    {"metric": "median_CD276_lognorm_positive_spots",

    {"metric": "max_CD276_lognorm", "value": float(df["CD276_lognorm"].max())},
]
san = pd.DataFrame(sanity)
san.to_csv(f"{TAB}/visium_c2l_abundance_sanity.csv", index=False)
print(san.to_string(index=False), flush=True)

log_run(step="diagnostics", status="ok", wall_time_s=round(time.time() - t0, 1),
        n_cells=len(df), detail=(f"mapping ELBO recovered ({n} epochs, "
                                 f"{elbo_first:,.0f}->{elbo_last:,.0f}); reference ELBO "
                                 f"unavailable (logger=False); sanity metrics written"))
print("DONE", flush=True)

Panel 4E / S5B step 3 (RE-RUN after an output-formatting defect): map cell-type
abundances onto the 22 Visium sections with cell2location.

Why this file exists
--------------------
The first 3,000-epoch mapping run (2026-10-21 15:08) trained successfully
(ELBO 104,060,600 -> 38,571,652) but its stored abundance tables are 100% NaN.
The cause is NOT the model: the export code built the output with

    pd.DataFrame(adata.obsm["means_cell_abundance_w_sf"],
                 index=adata.obs_names, columns=[f"mean_{c}" for c in factor_names])

The obsm DataFrame's columns are bare cell-type names, so the prefixed names
were interpreted as column SELECTION, not renaming, and every column became NaN.
A 5-epoch probe (visium_c2l_22_export_probe.py) shows obsm values are finite
(NaN fraction 0.0), the buggy construction gives NaN fraction 1.0, and a plain
rename gives 0.0. No checkpoint was saved (`enable_checkpointing=False`), so the
posterior cannot be re-exported; the mapping must be re-run. The configuration
here is identical to the original (3,000 epochs, batch 4096, lr 0.002,
N_cells_per_location=8, detection_alpha=20, section as batch, num_samples=200).
Only the export/validation code is corrected, and the model is saved so this
cannot happen again.

Outputs
-------
results/tables/visium_c2l_spot_abundances.parquet   (validated, overwritten)
data/processed/visium_c2l_abundances_small.h5ad     (validated, overwritten)
data/processed/c2l_mapping_model_rerun/             (saved model, audit)
logs/lightning/c2l_mapping_rerun/.../metrics.csv    (per-epoch ELBO)
"""
import os
import sys
import time
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import anndata as ad
import torch

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from visium_c2l_common import WORK, log_run  # noqa: E402

SEED = 42
ACCEL = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
BATCH_SIZE = int(os.environ.get("C2L_MAP_BS", "4096"))
MAX_EPOCHS = int(os.environ.get("C2L_MAP_EPOCHS", "3000"))
N_SAMPLES = int(os.environ.get("C2L_MAP_SAMPLES", "200"))
LR = 0.002
N_CELLS_PER_LOCATION = 8
DETECTION_ALPHA = 20

VIS = ("/mnt/beegfs/xqinag/projects/TheVirtualBiotech/runs/"
       "20261021-113551-round-2-of-the-b7-h3-cd276-case-ef6e8b35/work/"
       "single-cell-analyst/data/processed/visium_sections_qc.h5ad")
SIG = f"{WORK}/results/tables/c2l_reference_celltype_signatures_mean.csv"
TAB = f"{WORK}/results/tables"
PROC = f"{WORK}/data/processed"
MODEL_DIR = f"{PROC}/c2l_mapping_model_rerun"

        batch_size=BATCH_SIZE, device=ACCEL, n_cells=47448, n_genes=1926,
        detail=("Re-run forced by all-NaN stored abundances: output builder used "
                "prefixed column names as selection labels. Identical model config; "
                "only export fixed; model now saved."))

adata = ad.read_h5ad(VIS)
missing = [g for g in inf_aver.index if g not in adata.var_names]
print("signature genes missing from visium:", len(missing), flush=True)
pd.DataFrame({"gene_missing_from_visium": missing}).to_csv(
    f"{TAB}/visium_c2l_signature_genes_missing_from_visium.csv", index=False)
common = [g for g in inf_aver.index if g in adata.var_names]
inf_aver = inf_aver.loc[common]
print("signature genes shared with visium:", len(common), flush=True)

cd276_raw = adata[:, "CD276"].X
cd276_raw = (np.asarray(cd276_raw.todense()).ravel()
             if hasattr(cd276_raw, "todense") else np.asarray(cd276_raw).ravel())
lognorm_cd276 = adata[:, "CD276"].layers["lognorm"]
lognorm_cd276 = (np.asarray(lognorm_cd276.todense()).ravel()
                 if hasattr(lognorm_cd276, "todense")

adata = adata[:, common].copy()
adata.X = adata.X.astype(np.float32)
adata.obs["CD276_counts"] = cd276_raw
adata.obs["CD276_lognorm"] = lognorm_cd276
print("subset:", adata.shape, flush=True)

Cell2location.setup_anndata(adata, batch_key="section")
mod = Cell2location(adata, cell_state_df=inf_aver,
                    N_cells_per_location=N_CELLS_PER_LOCATION,
                    detection_alpha=DETECTION_ALPHA)
print(f"model: N_cells_per_location={N_CELLS_PER_LOCATION} "

import lightning.pytorch as pl  # noqa: E402

                                  name="c2l_mapping_rerun",

      f"steps/epoch={steps_per_epoch}", flush=True)

)

factor_names = list(adata.uns["mod"]["factor_names"])
mean_df = adata.obsm["means_cell_abundance_w_sf"].copy()
q05_df = adata.obsm["q05_cell_abundance_w_sf"].copy()

mean_df.columns = [f"mean_{c}" for c in factor_names]
q05_df.columns = [f"q05_{c}" for c in factor_names]

raw_mean = np.asarray(mean_df, dtype=float)
raw_q05 = np.asarray(q05_df, dtype=float)
print("mean nan frac", float(np.isnan(raw_mean).mean()),
      "min", float(np.nanmin(raw_mean)), "max", float(np.nanmax(raw_mean)), flush=True)
print("q05 nan frac", float(np.isnan(raw_q05).mean()), flush=True)
if not np.isfinite(raw_mean).all() or not np.isfinite(raw_q05).all():
    raise RuntimeError("Posterior export still contains non-finite abundances; refusing to write.")
if raw_mean.max() <= 0:
    raise RuntimeError("Posterior export is all-zero; refusing to write.")

meta_cols = ["section", "patient", "histology", "array_row", "array_col",
             "total_counts", "n_genes_by_counts", "qc_pass", "CD276_counts",
             "CD276_lognorm"]
out = pd.concat([adata.obs[meta_cols], mean_df, q05_df], axis=1)

small = ad.AnnData(

Panel 4E / S5B step 4: spatial-neighbourhood analysis of immune-cell abundance
around B7-H3 (CD276) high vs low Visium spots.

Definitions (pre-specified)
---------------------------
* Spot B7-H3 level: log1p(CP10K) of CD276 (NOT raw counts; depth-confounded).
* Stratification unit: SECTION. Each Visium section is an independent array
  from a single tissue block; pooling spots across sections before quartiling
  would let section-level depth/composition drive the split. Patients have up
  to 4 sections, so a patient-level split would mix tumour and adjacent-normal
  tissue. Sections are therefore stratified independently, and patient is used
  only to check donor-level consistency.
* high = CD276 lognorm > per-section 75th percentile; low = < 25th percentile;
  the middle 50% is excluded from the high-vs-low contrast (it is still used as
  a neighbour when computing neighbourhood means).
* Neighbourhood: k=6 nearest spots on the Visium hex lattice built from
  (array_row, array_col) with a hard radius of 2.05 coordinate units. On this
  lattice the six physical neighbours sit at 1.414 (diagonal) and 2.0
  (same-row); the next ring is >= 2.828. The radius therefore returns exactly
  the true neighbours and never crosses sections. Spots with 0 true neighbours
  (isolated QC-surviving spots) are excluded from the contrast and counted.
  Spots with 1-5 neighbours use the mean of the neighbours they have.
* Neighbour abundance = unweighted mean posterior cell-type abundance of the
  neighbouring spots, excluding the spot itself.
* Effect = (mean_neighbour_high - mean_neighbour_low) / mean_neighbour_low * 100.

Outputs
-------
results/tables/visium_neighborhood_immune_change.csv
results/tables/visium_neighborhood_robustness.csv
results/tables/visium_neighborhood_stratification.csv
results/figures/fig4e_neighborhood_immune_change.png/.pdf      (tumour)
results/figures/figs5b_neighborhood_immune_change.png/.pdf    (adjacent-normal)

import os
import sys
import time
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy.spatial import cKDTree

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from visium_c2l_common import WORK, log_run  # noqa: E402

SEED = 42
N_PERM = int(os.environ.get("C2L_NPERM", "1000"))
N_BOOT = int(os.environ.get("C2L_NBOOT", "1000"))
# Probe runs use a suffix so a timed small-N run can never masquerade as the

sections = sorted(df["section"].unique())

robust = pd.read_csv(f"{TAB}/visium_neighborhood_robustness.csv")

    r = robust[(robust.histology == histology) & (robust.metric == "mean")].copy()
    order = [c for c in IMMUNE + CONTEXT if c in set(r.cell_type)]
    r = r.set_index("cell_type").loc[order].reset_index()
    ps = per_sec[per_sec.histology == histology]

    gs = fig.add_gridspec(2, 2, width_ratios=[1.15, 1], height_ratios=[1, 1],

    ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[:, 0])
    y = np.arange(len(r))[::-1]
    colors = []
    for _, row in r.iterrows():

        colors.append(base if sig else "#d5d8dc")
    ax.barh(y, r["pooled_pct_change"], color=colors, edgecolor="none", height=0.7)
    ax.errorbar(r["pooled_pct_change"], y,
                xerr=[r["pooled_pct_change"] - r["bootstrap_ci_low"],
                      r["bootstrap_ci_high"] - r["pooled_pct_change"]],
                fmt="none", ecolor="black", elinewidth=1, capsize=2)
    ax.axvline(0, color="black", lw=0.8)
    ax.set_yticks(y)
    ax.set_yticklabels([f"{c}  (p={p:.3f})" if np.isfinite(p) else c

    ax.set_xlabel("% change in mean neighbour abundance\n(B7-H3-high vs B7-H3-low spots)", fontsize=9)
    ax.set_title("A  pooled effect (section-cluster bootstrap 95% CI)", fontsize=10, loc="left")
    for s in ["top", "right"]:
        ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)
    ax.text(0.99, 0.01, "red = immune (CI excludes 0)\ngrey = context / CI includes 0",

    ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 1])

    ax.axhline(0, color="black", lw=0.8)
    ax.set_xticks(x)
    ax.set_xticklabels(order, rotation=60, ha="right", fontsize=7)
    ax.set_ylabel("% change per section", fontsize=8)
    ax.set_title("B  per-section direction", fontsize=10, loc="left")
    ax.set_ylim(-100, 100)
    for s in ["top", "right"]:
        ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)

            else:
                vals.append(np.nan)
        ax.plot(np.arange(len(dnames)), vals, marker="o", ms=4, lw=1,

    ax.axhline(0, color="black", lw=0.8)
    ax.set_xticks(np.arange(len(dnames)))
    ax.set_xticklabels(dnames, fontsize=8)

    ax.set_title("C  per-donor direction", fontsize=10, loc="left")
    ax.set_ylim(-100, 100)
    for s in ["top", "right"]:
        ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)

    fig.suptitle(title, fontsize=12, fontweight="bold")
    fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/{outbase}.png", dpi=250, bbox_inches="tight")
    fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/{outbase}.pdf", bbox_inches="tight")

def make_figure(histology, outbase, title):

    order = [c for c in IMMUNE + CONTEXT if c in set(r.cell_type)]

    #   solid/hatched = CI excludes zero / CI includes zero
    face, edge, hatch = [], [], []

            row["bootstrap_ci_low"] > 0 or row["bootstrap_ci_high"] < 0)
        base = "#c0392b" if row.immune_compartment == "immune" else "#2471a3"
        face.append(base if sig else "white")
        edge.append(base)
        hatch.append("" if sig else "///")
    ax.barh(y, r["pooled_pct_change"], color=face, edgecolor=edge,
            hatch=hatch, linewidth=0.8, height=0.7)
    ax.errorbar(r["pooled_pct_change"], y,

    ax.axvline(0, color="black", lw=0.8)

        ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)

    ax.set_xticks(x)
    ax.set_xticklabels(order, rotation=60, ha="right", fontsize=7)
    ax.set_ylabel("% change per section", fontsize=8)
    ax.set_title("B  per-section direction", fontsize=10, loc="left")
    ax.set_ylim(-100, 100)
    for s in ["top", "right"]:
        ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)

    # C: per-donor
    ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 1])
    # donor x cell-type matrix from the per-section table
    dnames = sorted(ps["patient"].unique())
    for i, ct in enumerate(order):
        vals = []
        for d in dnames:
            sub = ps[(ps.cell_type == ct) & (ps.patient == d)]["pct_change"].dropna()
            if len(sub):
                vals.append(sub.mean())
            else:
                vals.append(np.nan)
        ax.plot(np.arange(len(dnames)), vals, marker="o", ms=4, lw=1,
                label=ct, color="#c0392b" if ct in IMMUNE else "#7f8c8d",
                alpha=0.8)
    ax.axhline(0, color="black", lw=0.8)

import os
import sys
import time
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.patches import Patch

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from visium_c2l_common import WORK, log_run  # noqa: E402

TAB = os.environ.get("C2L_TAB_DIR", f"{WORK}/results/tables")
FIG = os.environ.get("C2L_FIG_DIR", f"{WORK}/results/figures")
RUN_STATUS = os.environ.get("C2L_STATUS", "ok")

          "dendritic cell", "mast cell", "neutrophil", "plasma cell"]
CONTEXT = ["fibroblast", "epithelial cell", "endothelial cell"]

per_sec = pd.read_csv(f"{TAB}/visium_neighborhood_immune_change.csv")
robust = pd.read_csv(f"{TAB}/visium_neighborhood_robustness.csv")


def make_figure(histology, outbase, title):
    r = robust[(robust.histology == histology) & (robust.metric == "mean")].copy()
    order = [c for c in IMMUNE + CONTEXT if c in set(r.cell_type)]
    r = r.set_index("cell_type").loc[order].reset_index()
    ps = per_sec[per_sec.histology == histology]

    fig = plt.figure(figsize=(13, 8.5))
    gs = fig.add_gridspec(2, 2, width_ratios=[1.15, 1], height_ratios=[1, 1],
                          hspace=0.35, wspace=0.3)

    # A: pooled effect with CI
    ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[:, 0])
    y = np.arange(len(r))[::-1]

    #   fill colour  = compartment (red immune, blue context)
    #   solid/hatched = CI excludes zero / CI includes zero
    face, edge, hatch = [], [], []
    for _, row in r.iterrows():
        sig = np.isfinite(row["bootstrap_ci_low"]) and (
            row["bootstrap_ci_low"] > 0 or row["bootstrap_ci_high"] < 0)
        base = "#c0392b" if row.immune_compartment == "immune" else "#2471a3"
        face.append(base if sig else "white")
        edge.append(base)
        hatch.append("" if sig else "///")
    ax.barh(y, r["pooled_pct_change"], color=face, edgecolor=edge,
            hatch=hatch, linewidth=0.8, height=0.7)
    ax.errorbar(r["pooled_pct_change"], y,
                xerr=[r["pooled_pct_change"] - r["bootstrap_ci_low"],
                      r["bootstrap_ci_high"] - r["pooled_pct_change"]],
                fmt="none", ecolor="black", elinewidth=1, capsize=2)
    ax.axvline(0, color="black", lw=0.8)

    ax.set_title("A  pooled effect (section-cluster bootstrap 95% CI)", fontsize=10, loc="left")

    x = np.arange(len(order))
    for i, ct in enumerate(order):

        jitter = np.random.default_rng(0).normal(0, 0.06, len(vals))
        ax.scatter(np.full(len(vals), i) + jitter, vals, s=12, alpha=0.7,
                   color="#c0392b" if ct in IMMUNE else "#7f8c8d")
    ax.axhline(0, color="black", lw=0.8)
    ax.set_xticks(x)
    ax.set_xticklabels(order, rotation=60, ha="right", fontsize=7)
    ax.set_ylabel("% change per section", fontsize=8)
    ax.set_title("B  per-section direction", fontsize=10, loc="left")
    ax.set_ylim(-100, 100)
    for s in ["top", "right"]:
        ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)

    # C: pooled per-donor ratio, matching robustness.donor_pct_changes.
    #   ratio_d = 100 * sum_sections(mean_hi*n_hi - mean_lo*n_lo)
    #                   / sum_sections(mean_lo*n_lo)
    ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 1])
    dnames = sorted(ps["patient"].unique())
    for i, ct in enumerate(order):
        vals = []
        for d in dnames:
            sub = ps[(ps.cell_type == ct) & (ps.patient == d)]
            if len(sub):
                num = ((sub["mean_neighbor_high"] * sub["n_high"])
                       - (sub["mean_neighbor_low"] * sub["n_low"])).sum()
                den = (sub["mean_neighbor_low"] * sub["n_low"]).sum()
                vals.append(num / den * 100 if den > 0 else np.nan)
            else:
                vals.append(np.nan)
        ax.plot(np.arange(len(dnames)), vals, marker="o", ms=4, lw=1,
                label=ct, color="#c0392b" if ct in IMMUNE else "#2471a3",
                alpha=0.8)
    ax.axhline(0, color="black", lw=0.8)
    ax.set_xticks(np.arange(len(dnames)))
    ax.set_xticklabels(dnames, fontsize=8)
    ax.set_ylabel("pooled % change per donor\n(sum high-low / sum low)", fontsize=8)
    ax.set_title("C  per-donor direction (pooled ratio)", fontsize=10, loc="left")
    ax.set_ylim(-100, 100)
    for s in ["top", "right"]:
        ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)

    fig.suptitle(title, fontsize=12, fontweight="bold")
    fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/{outbase}.png", dpi=250, bbox_inches="tight")
    fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/{outbase}.pdf", bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close(fig)

print("DONE", flush=True)

composition (see the regenerated sums printed by script 31). It is therefore not
a valid composition summary on its own.

This script uses an additive endpoint instead: for every section,
    pp_diff = 100 * ( mean neighbour fraction in high spots

i.e. percentage points. The pooled estimate is the equal-weight mean of the
per-section pp differences (sections with >=3 high and >=3 low spots). Because
every spot's fractions are normalised by the same 14-compartment total, the pp
differences across ALL 14 compartments sum to zero by construction. The sum is
computed over the emitted rows (all 14) and asserted; the earlier version
emitted only 12 types, so the printed "~0" check was invalid.

same section bootstrap and within-section label-shuffle permutation as the
primary analysis. Two variants: all spots with >=1 neighbour, and only spots

"""
Multiple-testing correction for the spatial-neighbourhood endpoints.

The primary neighbourhood analysis (script 30) and the post-hoc composition
endpoints (scripts 31/32) report raw within-section label-shuffle permutation
p-values. No multiplicity correction was applied originally. This script adds
Benjamini-Hochberg FDR columns IN PLACE (same filenames, added columns) and
writes a small summary table.

Families
--------
* visium_neighborhood_robustness.csv: one BH pass per (histology, metric) over
  the 12 cell types; plus one global pass over all 48 primary rows.
* visium_neighborhood_composition_pp_difference.csv: one BH pass per
  (histology, variant, statistic) -- 14 tests for composition_pp, 1 for
  total_abundance_pct.
* visium_neighborhood_composition_sensitivity.csv: one BH pass per
  (histology, variant, endpoint) -- 14 tests for relative_composition,
  1 for total_abundance.

Caveat that no correction can fix: the permutation null shuffles high/low
labels WITHIN a section, destroying spatial autocorrelation, so the p-values
are anticonservative and the 1,000-permutation floor is p = 0.000999.

Output
------
the three tables above (extra columns) +
results/tables/visium_neighborhood_multiple_testing_summary.csv

import os
import sys
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from visium_c2l_common import WORK, log_run, checked_frame  # noqa: E402

TAB = f"{WORK}/results/tables"


def bh_fdr(pvals):
    """Benjamini-Hochberg q-values; NaNs are ignored but preserved."""
    p = np.asarray(pvals, dtype=float)
    ok = np.isfinite(p)
    q = np.full_like(p, np.nan)
    n = int(ok.sum())
    if n == 0:
        return q
    idx = np.where(ok)[0]
    order = idx[np.argsort(p[idx], kind="stable")]
    ranked = p[order]
    qvals = ranked * n / np.arange(1, n + 1)
    qvals = np.minimum.accumulate(qvals[::-1])[::-1]
    q[order] = np.clip(qvals, 0, 1)
    return q


def add_bh(df, family_cols, p_col="permutation_p", out_col="permutation_p_bh",
           family_name_col="bh_family"):
    df = df.copy()
    df[family_name_col] = df[family_cols].astype(str).agg("|".join, axis=1)
    df[out_col] = np.nan
    for fam, g in df.groupby(family_name_col, sort=False):
        df.loc[g.index, out_col] = bh_fdr(g[p_col].to_numpy(float))
    return df

r = pd.read_csv(f)
assert len(r) == 48, f"expected 48 primary robustness rows, got {len(r)}"
r = add_bh(r, ["histology", "metric"])

        "min_bh_q": float(g["permutation_p_bh"].min()),
    })

assert len(s) == 2 * 2 * 15, f"expected 60 sensitivity rows, got {len(s)}"
s = add_bh(s, ["histology", "variant", "endpoint"])
assert s["permutation_p_bh"].notna().all()
assert s.shape[1] == 15, s.shape
s.to_csv(f, index=False)
for fam, g in s.groupby("bh_family"):
    summary.append({
        "table": "visium_neighborhood_composition_sensitivity.csv",
        "family": fam, "n_tests": len(g),
        "n_p_at_floor": int((g["permutation_p"] <= 0.000999 + 1e-12).sum()),
        "n_bh_q_lt_0.05": int((g["permutation_p_bh"] < 0.05).sum()),
        "min_raw_p": float(g["permutation_p"].min()),
        "min_bh_q": float(g["permutation_p_bh"].min()),
    })

SUM_COLS = ["table", "family", "n_tests", "n_p_at_floor", "n_bh_q_lt_0.05",
            "min_raw_p", "min_bh_q"]
out = checked_frame(summary, SUM_COLS,
                    "visium_neighborhood_multiple_testing_summary")
out.to_csv(f"{TAB}/visium_neighborhood_multiple_testing_summary.csv", index=False)
print(out.to_string(index=False), flush=True)

log_run(step="neighborhood_multiple_testing", status="ok",
        detail=(f"BH-FDR added to robustness (48 rows; family=histology x metric), "
                f"composition pp and relative-composition tables (family="
                f"histology x variant x endpoint); {len(out)} families; "
                f"raw permutation p floor = 0.000999"))

# ---------------------------------------------------------- report-side checks
prim = r[r.metric == "mean"]
print("\nTumour mean-block raw p and BH q:", flush=True)
print(prim[prim.histology == "tumor"][
    ["cell_type", "pooled_pct_change", "permutation_p", "permutation_p_bh"]

        & (c.statistic == "composition_pp")][
    ["cell_type", "estimate", "permutation_p", "permutation_p_bh"]
].round(4).to_string(index=False), flush=True)
print("DONE", flush=True)

"""
Rebuild the 4B/4C pseudobulk DE top-gene table WITH a direction (sign) filter,
and extract the CD276 row across all contrasts into a small summary.

Why this script exists
----------------------
The delivered SOURCE table `scrna_pseudobulk_de_top_genes.csv` had no surviving
generating script and its "up"/"down" blocks were not sign-filtered: the "up"
block was simply the top-20 significant genes sorted by descending log2FC, so
it contained negative-log2FC genes (e.g. LUAD B cell primary: HINT1 -0.61 ...
ITM2B -1.05), and the LUAD B-cell paired block had identical up/down genes.

Fix: restrict to the DE thresholds already used by 06_pseudobulk_de.py
(padj < 0.05 AND |log2FC| > 0.5), then
  * up   = significant & log2FC > 0, sorted by log2FC descending
  * down = significant & log2FC < 0, sorted by log2FC ascending
and take at most TOP_N per direction. Rank is recomputed within the filtered
block. A `sign_filter_applied` column records the rule.

The large DE CSV (114 MB) is read READ-ONLY from the predecessor run; only the
small summaries are written into this run. Nothing large is copied.

Outputs
-------
results/tables/scrna_pseudobulk_de_top_genes.csv        (rebuilt, sign-filtered)
results/tables/scrna_cd276_de_summary.csv               (CD276 across contrasts)
"""
import os
import sys
import pandas as pd

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from visium_c2l_common import WORK, log_run, checked_frame  # noqa: E402

SOURCE_DE = ("/mnt/beegfs/xqinag/projects/TheVirtualBiotech/runs/"
             "20261021-113551-round-2-of-the-b7-h3-cd276-case-ef6e8b35/work/"
             "single-cell-analyst/results/tables/scrna_pseudobulk_de_luad_sclc.csv")
TAB = f"{WORK}/results/tables"
TOP_N = 20
PADJ = 0.05
MIN_ABS_LFC = 0.5

if not os.path.exists(SOURCE_DE):
    raise FileNotFoundError(f"SOURCE DE table not found (read-only input): {SOURCE_DE}")

use = ["histology", "cell_type", "analysis", "contrast", "gene", "baseMean",
       "log2FoldChange", "lfcSE", "pvalue", "padj", "n_disease_donors",
       "n_normal_donors", "significant"]
de = pd.read_csv(SOURCE_DE, usecols=use)
print("DE rows read:", de.shape, flush=True)
assert len(de) == 15 * 61497, f"unexpected DE row count: {len(de)}"

# Recompute the significance flag from the thresholds rather than trusting a
# stored column (they agree; this makes the filter explicit).
de["sig_recomputed"] = (de["padj"] < PADJ) & (de["log2FoldChange"].abs() > MIN_ABS_LFC)
assert (de["sig_recomputed"] == de["significant"]).all(), (
    "stored significance flag disagrees with padj<0.05 & |log2FC|>0.5")

# ------------------------------------------------------------- CD276 summary
cd = de[de["gene"] == "CD276"].copy()
assert len(cd) == 15, f"expected CD276 in all 15 contrasts, got {len(cd)}"
cd = cd.sort_values(["histology", "cell_type", "analysis"])
cd_out = cd[["histology", "cell_type", "analysis", "contrast", "gene",
             "baseMean", "log2FoldChange", "lfcSE", "pvalue", "padj",
             "significant", "n_disease_donors", "n_normal_donors"]]
cd_out = cd_out.rename(columns={"significant": "significant_at_padj0.05_absLFC0.5"})
cd_out = checked_frame(cd_out, list(cd_out.columns),
                       "scrna_cd276_de_summary")
cd_out.to_csv(f"{TAB}/scrna_cd276_de_summary.csv", index=False)
print("\nCD276 across 15 contrasts:", flush=True)
print(cd_out[["histology", "cell_type", "analysis", "baseMean",
              "log2FoldChange", "padj", "significant_at_padj0.05_absLFC0.5"]]
      .round(4).to_string(index=False), flush=True)
print("\nCD276 significant in any contrast:", int(cd_out[
    "significant_at_padj0.05_absLFC0.5"].sum()), "/", len(cd_out), flush=True)

# ------------------------------------------------------- sign-filtered top genes
sig = de[de["significant"]].copy()
rows = []
for (hist, ct, ana), g in sig.groupby(["histology", "cell_type", "analysis"],
                                      sort=False):
    up = g[g["log2FoldChange"] > 0].sort_values("log2FoldChange", ascending=False)
    dn = g[g["log2FoldChange"] < 0].sort_values("log2FoldChange", ascending=True)
    for direction, block in [("up", up.head(TOP_N)), ("down", dn.head(TOP_N))]:
        for rank, (_, r) in enumerate(block.iterrows(), start=1):
            rows.append({
                "histology": hist, "cell_type": ct, "analysis": ana,
                "direction": direction, "rank": rank, "gene": r["gene"],
                "log2FoldChange": r["log2FoldChange"], "lfcSE": r["lfcSE"],
                "padj": r["padj"], "baseMean": r["baseMean"],
                "n_disease_donors": r["n_disease_donors"],
                "n_normal_donors": r["n_normal_donors"],
            })

TOP_COLS = ["histology", "cell_type", "analysis", "direction", "rank", "gene",
            "log2FoldChange", "lfcSE", "padj", "baseMean", "n_disease_donors",
            "n_normal_donors"]
top = checked_frame(rows, TOP_COLS, "scrna_pseudobulk_de_top_genes")

# Fail-fast: no direction block may contain a wrong-sign gene.
bad_up = int(((top.direction == "up") & (top.log2FoldChange <= 0)).sum())
bad_dn = int(((top.direction == "down") & (top.log2FoldChange >= 0)).sum())
assert bad_up == 0 and bad_dn == 0, (bad_up, bad_dn)
# No gene may appear in both directions of the same block.
dupes = top.groupby(["histology", "cell_type", "analysis", "gene"])["direction"].nunique()
assert (dupes <= 1).all(), f"genes in both directions: {dupes[dupes > 1]}"
top.to_csv(f"{TAB}/scrna_pseudobulk_de_top_genes.csv", index=False)

print("\nSign-filtered top-gene blocks:", flush=True)
print(top.groupby(["histology", "cell_type", "analysis", "direction"])
      .size().to_string(), flush=True)
print("\nwrong-sign rows in rebuilt table:", bad_up + bad_dn, flush=True)

log_run(step="scrna_pseudobulk_de_top_genes_signfiltered", status="ok",
        detail=(f"Rebuilt from SOURCE 922,455-row DE CSV (read-only); "
                f"{len(top)} top-gene rows, up = log2FC>0, down = log2FC<0, "
                f"padj<{PADJ} and |log2FC|>{MIN_ABS_LFC}; up to {TOP_N}/direction; "
                f"CD276 summary written for all 15 contrasts"))
print("DONE", flush=True)

# Deprecated artefacts: all-NaN cell2location export

These two files are retained **for audit only**. They were produced by the first
3,000-epoch cell2location mapping run (2026-10-21 15:08) and every one of their
28 cell-abundance columns is NaN. They must not be used for any analysis,
figure, or claim. The validated replacements are listed under "Superseded by".

## Root cause

The export code built the abundance frame as

```python
pd.DataFrame(adata.obsm["means_cell_abundance_w_sf"],
             index=adata.obs_names,
             columns=[f"mean_{c}" for c in factor_names])
```

The `obsm` DataFrame already has **bare** cell-type names as its columns, so the
prefixed strings were interpreted by pandas as a **column selection list**, not a
rename. No stored column matched `mean_<type>`, so pandas emitted one all-NaN
column per requested label. The underlying posterior values in
`obsm["means_cell_abundance_w_sf"]` were finite (NaN fraction 0.0, confirmed by
`visium_c2l_22_export_probe.py`); only the export was broken. The checkpoint was
not saved (`enable_checkpointing=False`), so the posterior could not be
re-exported and the mapping was re-run. The re-run uses the same configuration
and fixes only the export (`mean_df.columns = [...]` on a copy). See
`code/scripts/visium_c2l_21_map_sections_rerun.py`.

A `checked_frame()` helper in `visium_c2l_common.py` now raises if a constructed
table has an unexpected column set, is empty, or is entirely NaN, so this class
of silent failure fails fast in future runs.

### `data/processed/deprecated_all_nan_export/visium_c2l_spot_abundances_all_nan_superseded.parquet`

| bytes | 926,080 |
| md5 | `483c11cc4d56cc2b69e4056162387e46` |
| shape | 47,448 rows x 38 columns |
| abundance columns | 28 (`mean_*` 14, `q05_*` 14) |
| NaN cells | 1,328,544 / 1,803,024 total |
| NaN in abundance columns | 1,328,544 / 1,328,544 (100%) |
| NaN in metadata columns | 0 |
| superseded by | `results/tables/visium_c2l_spot_abundances.parquet` |

| property | value |

| md5 | `7d54dffeb75e5b1bc6bcf7e3efb1d1f3` |
| obs shape | 47,448 x 38 |
| X shape | 47,448 x 1 (placeholder) |
| abundance columns | 28 (`mean_*` 14, `q05_*` 14) |
| NaN cells | 1,328,544 / 1,803,024 obs cells |
| NaN in abundance columns | 1,328,544 / 1,328,544 (100%) |

## Reporting note on the earlier arithmetic

An intermediate draft of the report described the all-NaN defect as affecting
"664,272 of 1,328,544 values" (47,448 x 14). That is the count for **one**
posterior statistic (mean **or** q05). Both are stored, so the correct count is

1,328,544 of 1,803,024 = 73.7% of all cells in the obs frame. The earlier figure
understated the defect by a factor of two. Revision 2 of the report uses the
corrected numbers.

# Training-history tables: which file to use

This note replaces three 6-byte, header-only CSVs
(`visium_c2l_mapping_history.csv`, `visium_c2l_mapping_history_rerun.csv`,
`c2l_reference_training_history.csv`) that each contained only the column name
`epoch` and no rows. A header-only file is not a training curve and must not be
cited as one. They have been deleted.

## Where the ELBO traces actually are

| model | trace available? | location | rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spatial mapping, original 3,000-epoch run | yes | `logs/c2l_mapping_elbo_metrics_3000epoch.csv` (columns `elbo_train,epoch,step`) | 3,000 |
| Spatial mapping, re-run (corrected export) | yes | `logs/lightning/c2l_mapping_rerun/3000ep/metrics.csv` | 3,000 |
| Reference signature RegressionModel | no | none written | 0 |

The derived statistics (first/last ELBO, last-10% slope, percent of total
decrease reached by 90% of epochs) are in
`results/tables/visium_c2l_training_convergence.csv`; the figure is
`results/figures/figs5_c2l_training_convergence.png`.

## Why the CSVs were empty

`mod.history` in scvi-tools 1.4 is populated from the Lightning logger. In the
re-run script a `CSVLogger` was attached, so the per-epoch values were written by
Lightning under `logs/lightning/`, but `mod.history` itself was empty at the time
the table was written. The reference model was trained with `logger=False`, so no
values were persisted anywhere.

`c2l_reference_training_history.csv` is therefore **not** recoverable: the model
completed 250/250 epochs (Lightning reported `max_epochs=250 reached`; 4,586.9 s,
18.3 s/epoch) but the loss values were never written. No curve is fabricated.

Script `visium_c2l_21_map_sections_rerun.py` now writes the history table only
when it has rows, and logs the Lightning metrics path otherwise.

abundances onto the 22 Visium sections with cell2location.

Why this file exists
--------------------
The first 3,000-epoch mapping run (2026-10-21 15:08) trained successfully

(NaN fraction 0.0), the buggy construction gives NaN fraction 1.0, and a plain
rename gives 0.0. No checkpoint was saved (`enable_checkpointing=False`), so the
posterior cannot be re-exported; the mapping must be re-run. The configuration
here is identical to the original (3,000 epochs, batch 4096, lr 0.002,
N_cells_per_location=8, detection_alpha=20, section as batch, num_samples=200).
Only the export/validation code is corrected, and the model is saved so this
cannot happen again.

Outputs
-------
results/tables/visium_c2l_spot_abundances.parquet   (validated, overwritten)
data/processed/visium_c2l_abundances_small.h5ad     (validated, overwritten)
data/processed/c2l_mapping_model_rerun/             (saved model, audit)
logs/lightning/c2l_mapping_rerun/.../metrics.csv    (per-epoch ELBO)

import os
import sys
import time
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import anndata as ad
import torch

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from visium_c2l_common import WORK, log_run  # noqa: E402

SEED = 42
ACCEL = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
BATCH_SIZE = int(os.environ.get("C2L_MAP_BS", "4096"))
MAX_EPOCHS = int(os.environ.get("C2L_MAP_EPOCHS", "3000"))
N_SAMPLES = int(os.environ.get("C2L_MAP_SAMPLES", "200"))
LR = 0.002
N_CELLS_PER_LOCATION = 8
DETECTION_ALPHA = 20

SIG = f"{WORK}/results/tables/c2l_reference_celltype_signatures_mean.csv"
TAB = f"{WORK}/results/tables"
PROC = f"{WORK}/data/processed"
# Self-contained: the QC h5ad is copied into this run (450 MB; byte-identical
# to the SOURCE copy, md5 a9066b064a85bc24cf710d7fba31e5db). No cross-run path.
VIS = f"{PROC}/visium_sections_qc.h5ad"
if not os.path.exists(VIS):
    raise FileNotFoundError(f"Visium QC input missing from LIVE run: {VIS}")
MODEL_DIR = f"{PROC}/c2l_mapping_model_rerun"

np.random.seed(SEED)
torch.manual_seed(SEED)

from cell2location.models import Cell2location  # noqa: E402

**Scope:** Ingest and QC the 22 E-MTAB-13530 LUAD Visium sections (12 tumor,
10 adjacent-normal). cell2location is deliberately **not** run here — this
hand-off file is the input for that later step.

**Result in one line:** 22/22 sections passed integrity checks and loaded;
**54,650 raw in-tissue spots → 47,448 QC-passed spots (86.8%)** across 12
tumor (29,185 → 27,826) and 10 adjacent-normal (25,465 → 19,622) sections.

---

## 1. Data source and files

- Accession **E-MTAB-13530** (BioStudies/ArrayExpress), De Zuani et al.,
  *Nat Commun* 2024 (PMID 38782901), cited by the Virtual Biotech paper as its
  Visium source. Provenance chain is in
  `config/visium_data_provenance.md`.
- Staged at
  `/mnt/beegfs/xqinag/projects/TheVirtualBiotech/runs/b7h3_round2_20261021/data/visium_raw/`
  (download log ends `DONE_ALL_VISIUM_DOWNLOADS`; all 44 data files non-zero).
- Space Ranger **1.1.0**, reference **GRCh38-2020-A**, 36,601 Gene Expression
  features per section.
- Section metadata (patient, age, sex, histology, stage) parsed from
  `E-MTAB-13530.sdrf.txt`, not inferred from names. All 22 target sections are
  `Characteristics[disease] = lung adenocarcinoma`.
  Histology is `tumor` for `_T` sections and `adjacent-normal` for `_B`
  sections (`Characteristics[sampling site]` = "normal tissue adjacent to
  tumor").

## 2. Verification and staging (22/22 pass)

Script: `code/scripts/visium_01_verify_extract.py`
Table: `results/tables/visium_file_verification.csv`

For every section the `.h5` was opened with h5py and checked for the complete
10x matrix schema (`matrix/{barcodes,data,indices,indptr,shape}` and
`matrix/features/{id,name,feature_type}`), internal shape consistency
(`shape[0]` = n features, `shape[1]` = n barcodes, `len(indptr)` = n barcodes+1,
`indptr[-1]` = nnz, `max(indices) < n features`), and non-negative integer
counts. Every `.tar` was opened as a POSIX tar (`tarfile` mode `r:`) and
required to contain all six Space Ranger spatial files:

`aligned_fiducials.jpg`, `detected_tissue_image.jpg`,
`scalefactors_json.json`, `tissue_hires_image.png`,
`tissue_lowres_image.png`, `tissue_positions_list.csv`.

The `-spatial.tar` files are uncompressed tar archives; extraction was done
with `tar -xf` (never `-xzf`). Each section was staged as

```
data/raw/visium_extracted/<section>/filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5
data/raw/visium_extracted/<section>/spatial/<six files>
```

so that `scanpy.read_visium` works directly on the directory.

**Outcome:** h5 22/22 OK, tar 22/22 OK, extraction 22/22 OK. No section was
dropped.

## 3. Barcode matching (perfect)

Table: `results/tables/visium_barcode_matching.csv`

| metric | value (22 sections) |
|---|---|
| matrix barcodes | 54,650 |
| array positions in positions files | 109,824 (= 22 × 4,992) |
| positions flagged in_tissue=1 | 54,650 |
| matrix barcodes absent from positions file | **0** |
| in-tissue positions absent from matrix | **0** |
| positions absent from matrix | 55,174 — all are `in_tissue=0` off-tissue positions |

Every filtered-matrix barcode matched an in-tissue spatial coordinate, and the

### Thresholds (stated a priori; NOT tuned to any reported count)

| filter | threshold | justification |
|---|---|---|
| total counts | ≥ 500 UMIs | below this a Visium spot is dominated by ambient/empty capture; standard Visium lower bound |
| detected genes | ≥ 200 | 200 genes is a conventional floor separating low-complexity/ambient spots from real tissue |
| mitochondrial % | ≤ 20% | >20% mitochondrial reads marks damaged/necrotic tissue; 20% is the common Visium upper bound (a 15% alternative is shown in sensitivity) |

Mitochondrial content is computed from the 13 `MT-` genes present in
GRCh38-2020-A. No upper count cap is applied: a Visium spot contains multiple
cells, so high UMI counts are legitimate.

## 1. Panel 4A — Germline credible sets + ENCODE-rE2G

### Methodology soundness
Two evidence streams are separated by construction, with an explicit table of what each stream can and cannot mean (`$W/genomics-analyst/results/reports/cd276_panel4a_report.md` §0). The germline stream is a verify-and-reuse of round-1 counts with two fresh region queries at ±250 kb and ±500 kb, plus a locus-interval-overlap sensitivity. The regulatory stream is a chunked parse of ENCODE-rE2G, selecting rows that are gene-linked **or** locus-overlapping, then restricting to ±500 kb. `code/scripts/04_validate_panel4a_outputs.py` asserts every headline count (7332, 839, 77, 762, 6, 1, 17/31/29, 9/16/29/78/122, 24/38/49, 201/195) and the report tokens. The report states that the paper's Figure 4A caption mixes germline association with regulatory prediction and declines to do so. The paper's "41 high-confidence elements" claim is **not** in `config/full_requirements.md` and is explicitly not used as a calibration target — correct handling.

"""
Audit the SDRF age / disease-staging fields for the 22 sections in this panel.

Why this exists
---------------
The Visium ingest report parsed `Characteristics[age]` and
`Characteristics[disease staging]` straight from E-MTAB-13530.sdrf.txt and copied
them into `.obs['age']` and `.obs['stage']`. A reviewer noticed that within a
single patient the age increments by one year per section and the AJCC M
category increments (M0, M1, M2, ...), which is not biologically possible: M2-M5
are not valid AJCC M categories. These fields describe the section, not the
patient, and must not be used as per-section covariates.

This script re-reads the SDRF (read-only), restricts to the 22 sections used in
the panel, and writes a section-level audit table plus a per-patient summary.
No data are modified; `.obs` columns are left as deposited.

Outputs
-------
results/tables/visium_sdrf_age_stage_integrity.csv
results/tables/visium_sdrf_age_stage_patient_summary.csv
"""
import os
import re
import sys

import anndata as ad
import pandas as pd

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from visium_c2l_common import WORK, log_run, checked_frame  # noqa: E402

SDRF = ("/mnt/beegfs/xqinag/projects/TheVirtualBiotech/runs/b7h3_round2_20261021/"
        "data/visium_raw/E-MTAB-13530.sdrf.txt")
H5AD = f"{WORK}/data/processed/visium_sections_qc.h5ad"
TAB = f"{WORK}/results/tables"

if not os.path.exists(SDRF):
    raise FileNotFoundError(f"SDRF not found (read-only input): {SDRF}")

sec = ad.read_h5ad(H5AD, backed="r").obs[
    ["section", "patient", "histology", "sampling_site", "age", "stage", "sex"]
].drop_duplicates().copy()
sections = sorted(sec["section"].unique())
assert len(sections) == 22, f"expected 22 sections, got {len(sections)}"

sdrf = pd.read_csv(SDRF, sep="\t", dtype=str)
need = ["Source Name", "Characteristics[original source name]",
        "Characteristics[age]", "Characteristics[disease]",
        "Characteristics[disease staging]", "Characteristics[sampling site]"]
missing = [c for c in need if c not in sdrf.columns]
assert not missing, f"SDRF missing columns: {missing}"

sub = sdrf[sdrf["Source Name"].astype(str).isin(sections)].copy()
assert len(sub) == 22, f"expected one SDRF row per section, got {len(sub)}"
sub = sub.set_index("Source Name")
assert set(sub.index) == set(sections), (
    f"SDRF sections != h5ad sections: {set(sub.index) ^ set(sections)}")

# Cross-check the h5ad copy against the SDRF verbatim.
sec = sec.set_index("section")
assert all(str(sec.loc[s, "age"]) == str(sub.loc[s, "Characteristics[age]"])
           for s in sections), "h5ad age disagrees with SDRF"
assert all(str(sec.loc[s, "stage"]) == str(sub.loc[s, "Characteristics[disease staging]"])
           for s in sections), "h5ad stage disagrees with SDRF"
assert all(str(sec.loc[s, "sampling_site"]) == str(sub.loc[s, "Characteristics[sampling site]"])
           for s in sections), "h5ad sampling site disagrees with SDRF"

M_RE = re.compile(r"M(\d+)")
rows = []
for s in sections:
    pat = sec.loc[s, "patient"]
    sib = sec[sec["patient"] == pat]
    age = int(sec.loc[s, "age"])
    stage = str(sec.loc[s, "stage"])
    m = M_RE.search(stage)
    m_cat = int(m.group(1)) if m else None
    rows.append({
        "patient": pat,
        "section": s,
        "histology": sec.loc[s, "histology"],
        "sdrf_original_source_name": sub.loc[s, "Characteristics[original source name]"],
        "sdrf_disease": sub.loc[s, "Characteristics[disease]"],
        "sdrf_sampling_site": sub.loc[s, "Characteristics[sampling site]"],
        "age": age,
        "age_min_in_patient": int(sib["age"].min()),
        "age_max_in_patient": int(sib["age"].max()),
        "age_varies_within_patient": bool(sib["age"].nunique() > 1),
        "stage": stage,
        "stage_n_distinct_in_patient": int(sib["stage"].nunique()),
        "stage_varies_within_patient": bool(sib["stage"].nunique() > 1),
        "stage_M_category": m_cat,
        "stage_M_invalid": bool(m_cat is not None and m_cat > 1),
        "usable_as_patient_level_covariate": False,
        "reason": ("age and stage differ between sections of the same patient; "
                   "M2-M5 are not valid AJCC M categories -> section-index "
                   "artefact, not patient metadata"),
    })
det = pd.DataFrame(rows)
COLS = ["patient", "section", "histology", "sdrf_original_source_name",
        "sdrf_disease", "sdrf_sampling_site", "age", "age_min_in_patient",
        "age_max_in_patient", "age_varies_within_patient", "stage",
        "stage_n_distinct_in_patient", "stage_varies_within_patient",
        "stage_M_category", "stage_M_invalid",
        "usable_as_patient_level_covariate", "reason"]
det = checked_frame(det, COLS, "visium_sdrf_age_stage_integrity")
assert len(det) == 22
assert det["usable_as_patient_level_covariate"].eq(False).all()
det.to_csv(f"{TAB}/visium_sdrf_age_stage_integrity.csv", index=False)

# Per-patient summary: does a single constant age exist anywhere?
summ = []
for pat, g in det.groupby("patient", sort=True):
    const_age = g["age"].nunique() == 1
    summ.append({
        "patient": pat,
        "n_sections": len(g),
        "n_tumor": int((g["histology"] == "tumor").sum()),
        "n_adjacent_normal": int((g["histology"] == "adjacent-normal").sum()),
        "age_min": int(g["age"].min()),
        "age_max": int(g["age"].max()),
        "age_span_years": int(g["age"].max() - g["age"].min()),
        "constant_age_within_patient": bool(const_age),
        "stages": "; ".join(sorted(g["stage"].unique())),
        "n_distinct_stages": int(g["stage"].nunique()),
        "has_invalid_M_category": bool(g["stage_M_invalid"].any()),
        "valid_patient_age_recoverable": bool(const_age),
    })
ps = pd.DataFrame(summ)
PS_COLS = ["patient", "n_sections", "n_tumor", "n_adjacent_normal", "age_min",
           "age_max", "age_span_years", "constant_age_within_patient", "stages",
           "n_distinct_stages", "has_invalid_M_category",
           "valid_patient_age_recoverable"]
ps = checked_frame(ps, PS_COLS, "visium_sdrf_age_stage_patient_summary")
assert len(ps) == 5
assert not ps["valid_patient_age_recoverable"].any(), (
    "a patient has a constant age; re-check the anomaly claim")
ps.to_csv(f"{TAB}/visium_sdrf_age_stage_patient_summary.csv", index=False)

print(ps.to_string(index=False), flush=True)
print("\ninvalid M categories:", int(det["stage_M_invalid"].sum()), "/", len(det),
      flush=True)
print("sections whose stage varies within patient:",
      int(det["stage_varies_within_patient"].sum()), "/", len(det), flush=True)

log_run(step="sdrf_metadata_integrity", status="ok",
        detail=("22/22 sections: age and/or stage vary between sections of the same "
                "patient; M2-M5 invalid AJCC categories; no patient has a constant "
                "age, so no patient-level age is recoverable; both fields flagged "
                "unusable as covariates"))
print("DONE", flush=True)

def checked_frame(rows, expected_columns, name):
    """Build a DataFrame and fail fast on the two bug classes seen in this run.

    1. Silent all-NaN construction (e.g. pandas `columns=` used as a rename).
    2. Column misalignment (a table whose columns are not what downstream code
       indexes by name).

    Parameters
    ----------
    rows : list[dict]
        Records to construct. A DataFrame may also be passed and is validated
        in place of construction.
    expected_columns : list[str]
        Exact expected column names, in order.
    name : str
        Human-readable artifact name used in the assertion message.
    """
    cols = list(expected_columns)
    df = rows if isinstance(rows, pd.DataFrame) else pd.DataFrame(rows)
    if list(df.columns) != cols:
        raise AssertionError(
            f"{name}: expected {len(cols)} columns {cols}, "
            f"got {len(df.columns)} {list(df.columns)}")
    if len(df) == 0:
        raise AssertionError(f"{name}: zero rows")
    if not df.notna().any().any():
        raise AssertionError(f"{name}: every value is NaN (silent export failure)")
    return df

            "step": step, "status": status,
            "max_epochs": max_epochs, "epochs_completed": epochs_completed,
            "batch_size": batch_size, "device": device,

        })

Audit the SDRF age / disease-staging fields for the 22 sections in this panel.

Why this exists
---------------
The Visium ingest report parsed `Characteristics[age]` and
`Characteristics[disease staging]` straight from E-MTAB-13530.sdrf.txt and copied
them into `.obs['age']` and `.obs['stage']`. A reviewer noticed that within a

category increments (M0, M1, M2, ...), which is not biologically possible: M2-M5
are not valid AJCC M categories. These fields describe the section, not the
patient, and must not be used as per-section covariates.

the panel, and writes a section-level audit table plus a per-patient summary.
No data are modified; `.obs` columns are left as deposited.

import sys

        "Characteristics[age]", "Characteristics[disease]",
        "Characteristics[disease staging]", "Characteristics[sampling site]"]

assert all(str(sec.loc[s, "sampling_site"]) == str(sub.loc[s, "Characteristics[sampling site]"])
           for s in sections), "h5ad sampling site disagrees with SDRF"

        "sdrf_disease": sub.loc[s, "Characteristics[disease]"],

        "stage_n_distinct_in_patient": int(sib["stage"].nunique()),
        "stage_varies_within_patient": bool(sib["stage"].nunique() > 1),

        "age_max_in_patient", "age_varies_within_patient", "stage",
        "stage_n_distinct_in_patient", "stage_varies_within_patient",
        "stage_M_category", "stage_M_invalid",

for pat, g in det.groupby("patient", sort=True):
    const_age = g["age"].nunique() == 1

        "n_sections": len(g),
        "n_tumor": int((g["histology"] == "tumor").sum()),

        "age_min": int(g["age"].min()),

        "age_span_years": int(g["age"].max() - g["age"].min()),
        "constant_age_within_patient": bool(const_age),
        "stages": "; ".join(sorted(g["stage"].unique())),

        "has_invalid_M_category": bool(g["stage_M_invalid"].any()),
        "valid_patient_age_recoverable": bool(const_age),
    })
ps = pd.DataFrame(summ)
PS_COLS = ["patient", "n_sections", "n_tumor", "n_adjacent_normal", "age_min",
           "age_max", "age_span_years", "constant_age_within_patient", "stages",
           "n_distinct_stages", "has_invalid_M_category",
           "valid_patient_age_recoverable"]
ps = checked_frame(ps, PS_COLS, "visium_sdrf_age_stage_patient_summary")
assert len(ps) == 5
assert not ps["valid_patient_age_recoverable"].any(), (

ps.to_csv(f"{TAB}/visium_sdrf_age_stage_patient_summary.csv", index=False)

print("\ninvalid M categories:", int(det["stage_M_invalid"].sum()), "/", len(det),

## 1.1 Metadata-integrity warning: SDRF age and disease staging

**Status: the section-level `age` and `stage` values in `.obs` must not be used
as patient covariates in any downstream model.**

Audit script: `code/scripts/visium_03_sdrf_metadata_integrity.py`
Tables: `results/tables/visium_sdrf_age_stage_integrity.csv` (22 sections),
`results/tables/visium_sdrf_age_stage_patient_summary.csv` (5 patients)

The deposited SDRF encodes one `Characteristics[age]` and one
`Characteristics[disease staging]` value **per section**, not per patient. Both
increment with the section index:

| patient | sections | age range | stages |
|---|---|---|---|
| P10 | 6 | 72–77 | T3N0M0 … T3N0M5 |
| P15 | 4 | 73–76 | T3N0M0 … T3N0M3 |
| P16 | 4 | 87–90 | T2bN0M0 (all four) |
| P24 | 4 | 52–55 | T3N0M0 … T3N0M3 |
| P25 | 4 | 64–67 | T3N0M0 … T3N0M3 |

- **No patient has a constant age** (all five have an age span of 3–5 years
  across 2–4 years of sections), so a valid patient-level age cannot be
  recovered from this field.
- **M2–M5 are not valid AJCC M categories.** 10 of 22 sections carry M2–M5
  (P10 four, P15 two, P24 two, P25 two); this is a data-entry artefact, not
  metastatic progression within a patient.
- Stage varies within 18 of 22 sections' patients (all except P16, whose four
  sections share T2bN0M0). Even there, age still varies.
- `.obs['age']` and `.obs['stage']` are retained **verbatim** for traceability
  and are identical to the SDRF (asserted in the audit script). They are
  labelled `usable_as_patient_level_covariate = False` in the audit table.
- Consequence: analyses in this panel are **not** adjusted for age or stage, and
  no per-section age/stage comparison is performed. Any synthesis statement that
  treats these as patient metadata would be unsupported.

"""
Annotate the reconstructed Census batch log and re-derive what is derivable.

Why this exists
---------------
`results/tables/scrna_census_batch_log.csv` was not captured from the tool. It
was written by `source_04_write_batch_log_reference.py`, which hardcodes the b1
row, takes b2/b3 cell counts from `n_cells_expected` in
`data/raw/metadata/luad_batch_definitions.csv`, hardcodes file sizes
(613.15 / 568.37 MB) and asserts `retry_count = 0`. The numbers are consistent
with the merge log, but the file is a reconstruction, not a record of what the
Census tool returned.

This script:
  1. reads the batch log and the predecessor merge log (read-only);
  2. re-derives each batch's returned cell count from the merge log's loaded
     shape -- the only surviving independent evidence;
  3. asserts the log's counts equal those shapes;
  4. adds explicit provenance columns so no reader mistakes the log for a raw
     tool record.

File sizes cannot be re-derived: the batch h5ad files no longer exist anywhere
in the run tree, so the sizes are hardcoded and flagged unverifiable.

Output
------
results/tables/scrna_census_batch_log.csv  (same rows + 4 provenance columns)
"""
import os
import re
import sys

import pandas as pd

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from visium_c2l_common import WORK, log_run, checked_frame  # noqa: E402

LOG_CSV = f"{WORK}/results/tables/scrna_census_batch_log.csv"
MERGE_LOG = ("/mnt/beegfs/xqinag/projects/TheVirtualBiotech/runs/"
             "20261021-113551-round-2-of-the-b7-h3-cd276-case-ef6e8b35/work/"
             "single-cell-analyst/logs/03_merge_qc_downsample.log")

if not os.path.exists(MERGE_LOG):
    raise FileNotFoundError(f"merge log not found (read-only evidence): {MERGE_LOG}")

bl = pd.read_csv(LOG_CSV)
assert len(bl) == 3 and set(bl["batch_id"]) == {"b1", "b2", "b3"}, bl.shape

# "batch01_576f193c_all.h5ad (90384, 61497) obs_names unique: True"
pat = re.compile(r"^(batch0(\d)_\S+\.h5ad)\s+\((\d+),\s+(\d+)\)")
derived = {}
with open(MERGE_LOG) as fh:
    for line in fh:

# SYNTHETIC FIXTURES — NOT REAL DATA

**Every file under `logs/synthetic_test/` is a synthetic test fixture.** None of
it is derived from E-MTAB-13530, cell2location, or any real specimen. Nothing
here may be cited, plotted, or quoted as a result.

## Why these files exist

The neighbourhood/composition scripts (30-32) and the figure script (41) were
exercised end-to-end on a synthetic abundance table before being run on real
data, to prove the code path and the fail-fast assertions worked. The outputs
were directed here, not to `results/`, so that a code test could not be mistaken
for a result.

## Inventory

| file | what it is |
|---|---|
| `visium_c2l_spot_abundances_SYNTHETIC.parquet` | synthetic spot x abundance table |
| `visium_c2l_abundances_small_SYNTHETIC.h5ad` | synthetic AnnData wrapper |

| `visium_neighborhood_immune_change_synthetic.csv` | same, explicitly suffixed |
| `visium_neighborhood_robustness.csv` | synthetic robustness output |
| `visium_neighborhood_robustness_synthetic.csv` | same, explicitly suffixed |
| `visium_neighborhood_stratification_synthetic.csv` | synthetic stratification output |
| `visium_neighborhood_edge_spot_sensitivity_synthetic.csv` | synthetic edge-spot output |
| `neighborhood_synthetic.log`, `panels_synthetic.log`, `neighborhood_figures_synthetic.log` | run logs of the synthetic test |
| `figures/` | figures rendered from the synthetic tables |

`SYNTHETIC` suffix (`visium_neighborhood_immune_change.csv`,

location under `logs/synthetic_test/` is the only marker. If you are looking for

import os
import sys
import time
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.colors import Normalize
import anndata as ad

RUN_STATUS = os.environ.get("C2L_STATUS", "ok")

IMMUNE = ["T cell", "B cell", "NK cell", "macrophage", "monocyte/myeloid",
          "dendritic cell", "mast cell", "neutrophil", "plasma cell"]
OTHER = ["epithelial cell", "malignant cell", "fibroblast", "endothelial cell", "stromal/other"]

COMP_COLORS = {
    "T cell": "#1f77b4", "B cell": "#aec7e8", "NK cell": "#17becf",
    "macrophage": "#d62728", "monocyte/myeloid": "#ff9896",
    "dendritic cell": "#9467bd", "mast cell": "#8c564b",
    "neutrophil": "#e377c2", "plasma cell": "#bcbd22",
    "epithelial cell": "#2ca02c", "malignant cell": "#98df8a",
    "fibroblast": "#ff7f0e", "endothelial cell": "#c49c94", "stromal/other": "#7f7f7f",
}

small = ad.read_h5ad(SMALL)
obs = small.obs.copy()
xy = small.obsm["spatial"]
cell_types = [c.replace("mean_", "") for c in obs.columns if c.startswith("mean_")]

obs["total_abundance"] = obs[[f"mean_{c}" for c in cell_types]].sum(axis=1)

    v = sub[col].to_numpy(dtype=float)

        vmax = np.percentile(v, 99) if np.isfinite(v).any() else 1.0
    vmax = max(vmax, 1e-9)
    sca = ax.scatter(sub["x"], sub["y"], c=v, s=2.2, cmap=cmap,
                     norm=Normalize(vmin=0 if vmin is None else vmin, vmax=vmax),
                     linewidths=0, rasterized=True)
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=8)
    ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([]); ax.invert_yaxis(); ax.set_aspect("equal")

def make_panel(histology, outbase, main_title):
    sub_h = obs[obs["histology"] == histology]
    sections = sorted(sub_h["section"].unique())
    # representative section = the one with the most spots
    rep = sub_h.groupby("section").size().idxmax()
    rep_df = sub_h[sub_h["section"] == rep]

    fig = plt.figure(figsize=(15, 11))
    gs = fig.add_gridspec(4, 5, height_ratios=[1.05, 1.05, 1.0, 1.0], hspace=0.35, wspace=0.28)

    # row 0: representative section, 5 maps
    maps = [("CD276_lognorm", "CD276 log1p(CP10K)"), ("immune_abundance", "total immune abundance"),
            ("T_cell_abundance", "T cell abundance"), ("macrophage_abundance", "macrophage abundance"),
            ("fibroblast_abundance", "fibroblast abundance")]
    for j, (col, lab) in enumerate(maps):
        ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, j])
        spatial_panel(ax, rep_df, col, f"{lab}\n{rep}", cmap="magma" if j == 0 else "viridis")
    fig.text(0.5, 0.965, main_title, ha="center", fontsize=13, fontweight="bold")
    fig.text(0.5, 0.935, f"representative section: {rep} (n={len(rep_df)} spots)", ha="center", fontsize=9)

    # rows 1-2: small multiples of total immune abundance for all sections
    from matplotlib.gridspec import GridSpecFromSubplotSpec
    sub_gs = GridSpecFromSubplotSpec(3, 4, subplot_spec=gs[1:3, :], hspace=0.18, wspace=0.12)
    vmax_imm = np.percentile(sub_h["immune_abundance"], 99)
    for k, sec in enumerate(sections):
        ax = fig.add_subplot(sub_gs[k // 4, k % 4])
        d = sub_h[sub_h["section"] == sec]
        spatial_panel(ax, d, "immune_abundance", f"{sec} (n={len(d)})", vmax=vmax_imm, cbar=(k == 0))

    # row 3: composition stacked bars
    ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[3, :])
    order = [c for c in IMMUNE + OTHER if c in cell_types]
    comp = sec_summary[sec_summary.histology == histology].set_index("section")[
        [f"mean_{c}" for c in order]].copy()
    comp.columns = order
    comp = comp.div(comp.sum(axis=1), axis=0) * 100
    bottom = np.zeros(len(comp))
    for ct in order:
        ax.bar(comp.index, comp[ct], bottom=bottom, color=COMP_COLORS.get(ct, "#333"),
               label=ct, width=0.75, linewidth=0)
        bottom += comp[ct].to_numpy()
    ax.set_ylabel("% of mean cell abundance", fontsize=8)
    ax.set_title("cell-type composition per section", fontsize=9)
    ax.tick_params(labelsize=7)
    ax.legend(ncol=5, fontsize=6, frameon=False, loc="upper center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.18))
    for s in ["top", "right"]:
        ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)

    fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/{outbase}.png", dpi=250, bbox_inches="tight")
    fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/{outbase}.pdf", bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close(fig)
    print("saved", outbase, flush=True)


make_panel("tumor", "fig4e_c2l_tumor",
           "Figure 4E - cell2location deconvolution of 12 LUAD tumour Visium sections")
make_panel("adjacent-normal", "figs5b_c2l_adjacent_normal",
           "Figure S5B - cell2location deconvolution of 10 matched adjacent-normal sections")

log_run(step=("panel_figures" if RUN_STATUS == "ok" else "panel_figures_synthetic_test"),

                                  f"{(obs['histology'] == 'adjacent-normal').sum()} adjacent-normal spots); "

## 6. Neighbourhood analysis: methods, results, robustness

### 6.1 Pre-specified definitions

* B7-H3 level: CD276 **log1p(CP10K)**, not raw counts.
* Stratification unit: **section** (each Visium array is independent; pooling
  spots across sections would let section-level depth/composition drive the
  split; patient-level splitting would mix histologies). high = CD276 above the
  per-section 75th percentile; low = below the 25th; the middle 50% is excluded
  from the contrast but still contributes as a neighbour.
* Neighbourhood: k=6 nearest spots on the Visium hex lattice
  (`array_row`,`array_col`), hard radius **2.05** coordinate units. The six
  physical neighbours are at 1.414 and 2.0; the next ring is >=2.828, so the
  radius returns exactly the true neighbours and never crosses sections. Spots
  with 0 neighbours (130; 37 tumour, 93 adjacent-normal) are excluded; spots
  with 1–5 neighbours (6,002) use the available neighbours.
* Neighbour abundance: unweighted mean posterior abundance of the neighbouring
  spots, self excluded.
* Effect: `(mean_neighbour_high - mean_neighbour_low) / mean_neighbour_low * 100`.
* Uncertainty: 1,000 section-cluster bootstrap resamples (95% percentile CI);
  significance: 1,000 within-section label shuffles (group sizes fixed).
* Reproducibility: seed 42; probe run with 20 permutations/bootstraps logged
  separately (`*_probe20.csv`); full run 22.9 s.

**Stratification reality check.** CD276 is zero in 76.2% of tumour spots
(range 66.3–86.9%) and 92.5% of adjacent-normal spots (83.7–98.2%). Ties at the
quartile boundary made `>q75` empty in **22/22 sections**, so the deterministic
rank fallback (top/bottom 25% by CD276 rank) was used throughout. Consequently:
the high group is CD276-positive in 87.3% of tumour spots (range 52.3–100%) but
only **30.0%** of adjacent-normal spots (7.3–65.2%); the low group is 100% CD276
zero. The adjacent-normal contrast is therefore weak and near the detection
floor. Median total counts are 1.76x higher in tumour high vs low spots (9,164
vs 5,211) and 1.28x higher in adjacent-normal (3,249 vs 2,540); per-section
Spearman CD276 vs total counts averages 0.295 in tumour and 0.150 in
adjacent-normal.

def bh_fdr(pvals):

    p = np.asarray(pvals, dtype=float)

    q[order] = np.clip(qvals, 0, 1)

# Panels 4E and S5B: cell2location deconvolution and spatial neighbourhood of B7-H3 (CD276) in LUAD

**Revision 2** (2026-10-21). Supersedes Revision 1 of the same path.
Run: `20261021-204038-round-2-of-the-b7-h3-cd276-case-a9b7a6f8`
Agent: single-cell-analyst

All paths below are relative to `work/single-cell-analyst/`.

**What changed in Revision 2.** Every quantitative sentence below was checked
against a delivered table. The corrected statements and their old -> new values
are listed in the Revision 2 changelog immediately after this header. The
underlying model fits were not re-run except for the forced mapping re-run
described in Section 1; no DE, LIANA, TCGA or reference-model computation was
re-executed.

## Revision 2 changelog

| # | Location | Revision 1 statement | Revision 2 statement | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | §1 | Abundance files had "664,272 / 664,272 NaN" | **1,328,544 / 1,328,544** NaN abundance values (47,448 x 28 mean+q05; 100% of abundance columns, 73.7% of all obs cells) | `data/processed/deprecated_all_nan_export/MANIFEST.md`; `visium_c2l_run_log.csv` correction rows |
| 2 | §4 | "Tumour sections are denser ... than adjacent-normal" | Tumour has **higher sequencing depth** (median total counts 4,215 vs 2,123 per spot) and more CD276-positive spots (23.8% vs 7.5%), but **slightly lower estimated cell abundance** (median of section means 6.42 vs 7.13) | `visium_c2l_section_summary.csv`; `visium_c2l_spot_abundances.parquet` |
| 3 | §6.1 | "`>q75` empty in 22/22 sections" | **`<q25` empty in 22/22**; `n_cd276_gt_q75` is 15-617 in every section. The rank fallback is triggered by the empty low tail, not the high tail | `visium_c2l_cd276_stratification_audit.csv` |
| 4 | §6.1 | "Median total counts are 1.76x higher ... (9,164 vs 5,211)" | Those are **means of per-section means** (1.76x). Median of per-section medians: **7,337 vs 3,676 (2.00x)**. Adjacent-normal: mean-of-means 3,249 vs 2,540 (1.28x); median-of-medians 2,326 vs 1,945 (1.20x) | `visium_c2l_cd276_stratification_audit.csv` (`mean_` and `median_total_counts_*`) |
| 5 | §6.4 | Composition sums "across the 11 types": tumour -38.1%, adjacent-normal +3.1% | Composition covers **14 compartments**. Pooled percent-change sums: tumour **-40.1%**, adjacent-normal **+3.2%**. The additive pp endpoint sums to **0.0 exactly** (asserted < 1e-6) | `visium_neighborhood_composition_sensitivity.csv`; `visium_neighborhood_composition_pp_difference.csv` |
| 6 | §6.4 | Equal-weight tumour total abundance +12.02% (-1.12, 25.41); adjacent-normal +4.78% (3.04, 6.60); six-neighbour tumour +37.84% (2.14, 94.72); adjacent-normal +5.98% (-1.22, 13.19) | **+12.02% (-1.66, 25.99); +4.78% (3.05, 6.71); +37.83% (2.59, 100.05); +5.98% (-1.39, 13.11)**. Point estimates unchanged; CIs shifted slightly because adding two compartments to the loop changed the bootstrap RNG stream | `visium_neighborhood_composition_pp_difference.csv` |
| 7 | §6.2, §6.4 | "ns" used without definition; neutrophil +0.16 pp labelled "ns" despite p at the permutation floor | "ns" removed. Neutrophil +0.16 pp (95% CI **-0.10 to 0.45**; BH q 0.0013): significant by permutation but the **CI includes 0**, so not an enrichment. Every "ns" is now an explicit CI or q value | `visium_neighborhood_composition_pp_difference.csv` |
| 8 | §6.4 | 12 immune/context compartments only | **All 14** reported: malignant **+3.79 pp** (2.27, 5.35; 12/12 sections, 5/5 donors) and stromal/other **-0.97 pp** (-1.46, -0.51) added to the tumour all-spot table; the same two are added to the six-neighbour table (+6.31 and -1.50 pp) | `visium_neighborhood_composition_pp_difference.csv` |
| 9 | §6.4 | Six-neighbour macrophage "permutation p 0.105" | **p = 0.091 raw, BH q = 0.116** (not significant at 0.05 after correction) | `visium_neighborhood_composition_pp_difference.csv` |
| 10 | §6 | No multiplicity correction | **Benjamini-Hochberg FDR** added within five defined families; q columns added to all three neighbourhood tables | `visium_neighborhood_multiple_testing_summary.csv` |
| 11 | §6, §7 | Permutation p reported without caveat | **Spatial-autocorrelation caveat** added: the within-section label shuffle destroys spatial structure, so the null is too narrow and p is anticonservative; floor 1/1001 = 0.000999 | §6.5, §7 |
| 12 | §6, §7 | Donor consistency reported as "x/5 donors" without caveat | **Donor-cluster caveat** added: only 5 donors per histology, sections within a donor are not independent, and the section bootstrap overstates precision relative to a donor-level analysis | §6.5, §7 |
| 13 | §8 | Bottom line emphasised only DC enrichment and endothelial depletion | Bottom line now also states the **donor-concordant depletions** of NK, macrophage, monocyte and mast cells, and distinguishes them from the density-driven absolute increases | §8; `visium_neighborhood_composition_pp_difference.csv` |
| 14 | Figure 4E/S5B panels | Panel C estimator did not reconcile with `donor_pct_changes`; Panel A legend conflated colour and significance | Panel C now **reconstructs the pooled per-donor ratio** from per-section sums and matches `donor_pct_changes` (max difference 0.05 pp); Panel A legend separates **colour = compartment** from **hatch = CI includes 0** | `code/scripts/visium_c2l_41_neighborhood_figures.py`; `visium_neighborhood_robustness.csv` |
| 15 | §1 | No normal-tissue CD276 expression context | Added: CD276 is detected in **normal lung macrophages at 36.53%** (3,011 cells, mean log expression 0.260), comparable to LUAD fibroblasts (30.84%, 3,411 cells, 0.329) and SCLC fibroblasts (35.25%, 244 cells, 0.401) | `scrna_cd276_expression_by_celltype.csv` |
| 16 | §2 | Epoch reduction asserted as "deliberate CPU-budget reduction" without measured throughput | Added measured **0.192-0.216 s/step, 12 steps/epoch, 2.3-2.6 s/epoch**; 3,000 epochs = 1.9-2.2 h, 10,000 epochs would be 6.4-7.2 h for a further 0.04% ELBO decrease | `c2l_mapping_full.log`, `c2l_mapping_rerun.log`, `visium_c2l_training_convergence.csv` |
| 17 | §1, §7 | SDRF age/stage not flagged | Added: SDRF age and stage vary between sections of the same patient and M2-M5 are invalid; **unusable as covariates** | `visium_sdrf_age_stage_integrity.csv`; `visium_ingest_qc_log.md` §1.1 |
| 18 | §3 | Header-only `visium_c2l_mapping_history*.csv` implied a trace | The 6-byte files were deleted; Read the ELBO trace from `logs/c2l_mapping_elbo_metrics_3000epoch.csv` and the re-run Lightning metrics | `results/tables/visium_c2l_mapping_history_README.md` |
| 19 | §1 | Deprecated all-NaN files preserved without a manifest | Manifest with size, shape, NaN count, md5, bug cause and superseding file | `data/processed/deprecated_all_nan_export/MANIFEST.md` |

---

## 1. Data provenance and QC

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Dataset | E-MTAB-13530 (De Zuani et al., *Nat Commun* 2024), 10x Visium LUAD |
| Reference | Space Ranger 1.1.0, GRCh38-2020-A, 36,601 genes |
| Sections used | 22: 12 tumour (P10 T1-T4; P15, P16, P24, P25 T1-T2) and 10 matched adjacent-normal (B1/B2 per donor) |
| QC-passed spots | 47,448 total (27,826 tumour; 19,622 adjacent-normal) |
| Spot QC (a priori) | >=500 UMIs, >=200 genes, <=20% mitochondrial reads |
| Deconvolution reference | 384,806 cells, 14 cell types, 2,000 HVGs; CD276 excluded to avoid circularity; SCLC excluded |
| Mapping inputs | 1,926 shared genes; `N_cells_per_location=8`, `detection_alpha=20`, learning rate 0.002, section as batch, `num_samples=200` |
| Deconvolved outputs | `mean_*` and `q05_*` posterior cell abundance for 14 cell types |

The spot abundance matrix is `results/tables/visium_c2l_spot_abundances.parquet`
(47,448 rows x 38 columns: 14 mean abundances, 14 q05 abundances, depth/QC and
CD276 columns). It contains **0 NaN** values; mean abundance range
1.05e-4 to 33.40. The mapping is saved under
`data/processed/c2l_mapping_model_rerun/`.

**Forced deviation from the instruction not to re-map.** The abundance files
inherited from the source run contained **1,328,544 / 1,328,544 NaN** abundance
values: 47,448 spots x 28 columns (14 `mean_*` + 14 `q05_*`). That is 100% of the
abundance columns and 1,328,544 / 1,803,024 = 73.7% of all values in the obs
frame. Revision 1 reported 664,272 / 664,272, which counted only one of the two
posterior statistics; the correction is recorded in the deprecation manifest and
in the run log.

The cause was the export code
`pd.DataFrame(adata.obsm[...], columns=[f"mean_{c}" ...])`, which treats the
prefixed names as a column **selection list** rather than a rename. A 5-epoch
API probe (`code/scripts/visium_c2l_22_export_probe.py`) proved the underlying
obsm values were finite (NaN fraction 0.0) and that the corrected construction
produced 0 NaN. No model checkpoint existed, so the mapping was re-run with the
identical configuration and a corrected export
(`code/scripts/visium_c2l_21_map_sections_rerun.py`). The invalid files are
preserved under `data/processed/deprecated_all_nan_export/`, with a manifest
recording size, shape, NaN count, md5 and the superseding file. **No DE, LIANA,
TCGA or reference-model computation was re-run.** The 4B/4C DE top-gene table
and the CD276 DE summary were rebuilt read-only from the existing 922,455-row DE
result, but the DE model itself was not re-fit.

**CD276 expression context (added in Revision 2).**
`results/tables/scrna_cd276_expression_by_celltype.csv` shows that CD276 is not
tumour-restricted at the transcript level: normal lung macrophages have the
highest detection fraction in the atlas at **36.53%** (3,011 cells, mean log
expression 0.260), comparable to LUAD fibroblasts (**30.84%**, 3,411 cells,
0.329) and SCLC fibroblasts (**35.25%**, 244 cells, 0.401). Any statement that
CD276 is tumour-specific is contradicted by this panel's own table.

**Metadata-integrity warning.** SDRF `age` and `stage` vary between sections of
the same patient and contain invalid AJCC M categories (M2-M5); no patient has a
constant age. These fields are retained verbatim in `.obs` but are unusable as
covariates. Details and the section-level table are in
`results/reports/visium_ingest_qc_log.md` §1.1 and
`results/tables/visium_sdrf_age_stage_integrity.csv`.

---

## 2. Compute environment and epoch deviations

| Model | Paper | Here | Wall time |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reference regression | 250 epochs, H100 | 250/250 epochs, CPU | 4,586.9 s (18.3 s/epoch) |
| Spatial mapping | 10,000 epochs, H100 | 3,000/3,000 epochs, CPU (original and re-run) | 7,134.4 s original; 7,769.7 s train + 204.5 s export re-run |

* Environment: cell2location 0.1.5, scvi-tools 1.4.2, PyTorch 2.12.0, **CPU
  only**. CUDA use was blocked by the run policy, not by availability of a GPU
  request; no GPU run was attempted.
* **Measured throughput (added in Revision 2).** The mapping has 47,448 spots,
  batch size 4,096, and **12 steps/epoch**. Measured per-step time was
  **0.192 s** in the original run and **0.216 s** in the re-run, i.e.
  **2.3-2.6 s/epoch**. 3,000 epochs therefore cost 6,926-7,770 s (1.9-2.2 h).
  Extrapolating linearly, the paper's 10,000 epochs would have cost
  **23,040-25,920 s (6.4-7.2 h)**, 3.3x longer, for a further ELBO decrease of
  only **0.04%** (Section 3).
* **Epoch rationale.** The reduction from 10,000 to 3,000 epochs is a
  deliberate CPU-budget decision, not an accidental truncation. It is justified
  by the convergence diagnostics: 99.96% of the total ELBO decrease had occurred
  by epoch 2,700 and the last-10% slope was only -137.6 ELBO units/epoch on a
  38.6M ELBO (-0.00036%/epoch).
* **Likely effect.** Posterior abundances should be close to converged, but
  cell-type-specific calibration may differ modestly from a 10,000-epoch model.
  Absolute abundances are not directly comparable to the paper's; within-study
  high-vs-low contrasts are the appropriate readout.

---

## 3. Model diagnostics

`results/tables/visium_c2l_training_convergence.csv`,
`results/figures/figs5_c2l_training_convergence.png`

| Model | Epochs | ELBO first | ELBO last | Last-10% mean (SD) | Rel. change last 10% | Slope/epoch | % decrease by 90% epoch |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mapping, original | 3,000 | 104,060,600 | 38,571,652 | 38,595,387 (17,552) | -0.075% | -137.6 | 99.956% |
| Mapping, re-run | 3,000 | 104,199,816 | 38,557,988 | 38,567,153 (17,353) | -0.042% | -131.3 | 99.976% |
| Reference regression | 250 | - | - | - | - | - | - |

The re-run final ELBO differs from the original by **-0.04%**, confirming that
the re-map reproduced the original fit rather than changing the model.

**Reference ELBO is UNAVAILABLE, not omitted.** The 250/250 epochs completed
(Lightning `max_epochs=250 reached`; 4,586.9 s; 18.3 s/epoch), but scvi-tools
1.4 populates `model.history` only when a Lightning logger is attached, and the
reference was trained with `logger=False`. No loss values were written. No curve
is fabricated; the figure states this explicitly. The mapping trace was recovered
from the original run's CSVLogger and is stored as
`logs/c2l_mapping_elbo_metrics_3000epoch.csv`. The per-epoch trace of the re-run
is in `logs/lightning/c2l_mapping_rerun/3000ep/metrics.csv`. The previous
header-only `visium_c2l_mapping_history*.csv` files have been deleted; see
`results/tables/visium_c2l_mapping_history_README.md`.

Abundance sanity checks (`results/tables/visium_c2l_abundance_sanity.csv`):

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Spots | 47,448 |
| Spearman total abundance vs total counts | **0.402** |
| Spearman immune abundance vs total counts | **0.304** |
| Spearman total abundance vs n genes | 0.387 |
| Median total abundance / spot | 5.365 |
| Median immune abundance / spot | 2.562 |
| Spots with total abundance < 1 | 0.004% |
| Spots with immune abundance < 1 | 3.064% |
| Spots with CD276 count 0 | **83.32%** |
| Median CD276 log1p(CP10K), positive spots | 0.991 |
| Max CD276 log1p(CP10K) | 3.957 |

The positive abundance-depth correlation is expected for deconvolution and is
the reason the composition sensitivity in Section 6 was added.

---

## 4. Per-section QC and abundance summary

`results/tables/visium_c2l_section_summary.csv` (22 rows; one per section).
`results/tables/visium_c2l_cd276_stratification_audit.csv` (stratification
