## 6. Neighbourhood analysis: methods, results, robustness

### 6.1 Pre-specified definitions

* B7-H3 level: CD276 **log1p(CP10K)**, not raw counts.
* Stratification unit: **section** (each Visium array is independent; pooling
  spots across sections would let section-level depth/composition drive the
  split; patient-level splitting would mix histologies). high = CD276 above the
  per-section 75th percentile; low = below the 25th; the middle 50% is excluded
  from the contrast but still contributes as a neighbour.
* Neighbourhood: k=6 nearest spots on the Visium hex lattice
  (`array_row`,`array_col`), hard radius **2.05** coordinate units. The six
  physical neighbours are at 1.414 and 2.0; the next ring is >=2.828, so the
  radius returns exactly the true neighbours and never crosses sections. Spots
  with 0 neighbours (130; 37 tumour, 93 adjacent-normal) are excluded; spots
  with 1-5 neighbours (6,002; 2,783 tumour, 3,219 adjacent-normal) use the
  available neighbours.
* Neighbour abundance: unweighted mean posterior abundance of the neighbouring
  spots, self excluded.
* Effect: `(mean_neighbour_high - mean_neighbour_low) / mean_neighbour_low * 100`.
* Uncertainty: 1,000 section-cluster bootstrap resamples (95% percentile CI);
  significance: 1,000 within-section label shuffles (group sizes fixed).
* Reproducibility: seed 42; probe run with 20 permutations/bootstraps logged
  separately (`*_probe20.csv`); full run 23.8 s.

**Stratification reality check.** CD276 is zero in 76.2% of tumour spots
(range 66.3-86.9%) and 92.5% of adjacent-normal spots (83.7-98.2%). Ties at the
lower quartile made **`<q25` empty in 22/22 sections** (`n_cd276_gt_q75` is
15-617 in every section, so the high tail is populated), and the deterministic
rank fallback (top/bottom 25% by CD276 rank) was used throughout. Revision 1
stated the opposite tail; corrected. Consequently: the high group is
CD276-positive in 87.3% of tumour spots (range 52.3-100%) but only **30.0%** of
adjacent-normal spots (7.3-65.2%); the low group is 100% CD276 zero. The
adjacent-normal contrast is therefore weak and near the detection floor.

**Depth balance (labels corrected in Revision 2).** The **mean of the
per-section mean total counts** is 1.76x higher in tumour high vs low spots
(**9,164 vs 5,211**) and 1.28x higher in adjacent-normal (**3,249 vs 2,540**).
The **median of the per-section median total counts** is 7,337 vs 3,676 (2.00x)
in tumour and 2,326 vs 1,945 (1.20x) in adjacent-normal. Revision 1 labelled the
first pair "median"; both quantities are now reported with their correct
statistic. Per-section Spearman CD276 vs total counts averages 0.295 in tumour
and 0.150 in adjacent-normal (section medians 0.311 and 0.161).

### 6.5 Multiplicity, spatial autocorrelation and donor clustering

**(a) Multiplicity.** Revision 1 reported raw within-section permutation
p-values with no correction. Revision 2 adds Benjamini-Hochberg FDR within five
pre-declared families, and all three neighbourhood tables now carry
`permutation_p_bh`. Families: absolute abundance = histology x metric (12 tests
per family); additive composition pp = histology x variant x `composition_pp`
(14 tests); relative composition = histology x variant x `relative_composition`
(14 tests); each `total_abundance` endpoint is a single-test family; and the
robustness table also gets a global 48-test pass
(`permutation_p_bh_global48`). Summary counts are in
`results/tables/visium_neighborhood_multiple_testing_summary.csv`.

| Family | n tests | q_BH < 0.05 | min raw p |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tumour absolute abundance (mean) | 12 | 11 | 0.0010 |
| Adjacent-normal absolute abundance (mean) | 12 | 12 | 0.0010 |
| Tumour composition pp, all spots | 14 | 12 | 0.0010 |
| Adjacent-normal composition pp, all spots | 14 | 5 | 0.0010 |
| Tumour composition pp, six-neighbour | 14 | 8 | 0.0010 |
| Adjacent-normal composition pp, six-neighbour | 14 | 0 | 0.126 |
| Tumour relative composition, all spots | 14 | 11 | 0.0010 |
| Adjacent-normal relative composition, all spots | 14 | 8 | 0.0010 |
| Tumour relative composition, six-neighbour | 14 | 5 | 0.0010 |
| Adjacent-normal relative composition, six-neighbour | 14 | 0 | 0.078 |

The correction does not rescue the fragile endpoints: the tumour six-neighbour
composition family retains 8/14 signals driven by the malignant/endothelial/
fibroblast axis, and the adjacent-normal six-neighbour family retains none
(min raw p = 0.126). The plasma-cell absolute increase (p = 0.149) and the
six-neighbour macrophage depletion (q = 0.116) remain non-significant.

**(b) Spatial autocorrelation.** The permutation null shuffles high/low labels
**within a section**, which destroys the spatial autocorrelation of both CD276
and the neighbour abundances. The resulting null is therefore too narrow and the
permutation p-values are **anticonservative**. This is a property no
multiplicity correction can fix. The 1,000-permutation floor is
1/1001 = 0.000999, and 9-11 of the 12 absolute-abundance tests sit exactly at
that floor; those q values should be read as "p <= 1/1001", not as precise
probabilities. The section-cluster bootstrap is the more defensible uncertainty
statement, and it is the one used for the CIs quoted above.

**(c) Donor clustering.** There are only **5 donors per histology**. "3/5" or
"4/5 donors positive" is a descriptive consistency count, not a formal test. The
bootstrap resamples sections, not donors, so it treats sections from one patient
as independent and **overstates precision relative to a donor-cluster analysis**.
The per-donor values are reported in the `donor_pct_changes` column of
`visium_neighborhood_robustness.csv` and in Figure 4E/S5B panel C so a
donor-level analysis can be reconstructed.

## 7. Limitations

1. **Depth confounding.** Total and immune abundance correlate with total
   counts (rho 0.40 and 0.30); high-CD276 spots are deeper in tumour
   (mean-of-section-means 9,164 vs 5,211 counts; median-of-medians 7,337 vs
   3,676). Composition and density endpoints mitigate but do not eliminate
   this; a count-matched or depth-regressed design would be stronger.
2. **Sparsity / weak contrast.** CD276 is zero in 83% of all spots; the rank
   fallback was used in 22/22 sections because `<q25` was empty. In
   adjacent-normal, the "high" group is only 30% CD276-positive, so that panel
   tests a shallow gradient and is close to noise.
3. **Edge dependence.** Most tumour immune effects change sign when 1-5
   neighbour spots are excluded; the primary estimate is not robust to spot
   inclusion.
4. **No independent validation.** Results are from one dataset (E-MTAB-13530);
   no held-out section or external Visium cohort was used.
5. **Model approximation.** Mapping used 3,000 epochs (paper 10,000) and CPU;
   the ELBO is flat, but absolute abundances are model-dependent and should not
   be compared across studies.
6. **Reference ELBO unavailable** (logger=False), so reference convergence can
   only be inferred from the reported 250/250 epochs and wall time.
7. **Post-hoc endpoints.** Composition and total-abundance sensitivity analyses
   were added after observing the depth and edge sensitivity; they are
   exploratory, not pre-registered. BH correction reduces but does not remove
   the exploratory-inference problem.
8. **Permutation null ignores spatial autocorrelation**, so p-values are
   anticonservative (Section 6.5b).
9. **Only 5 donors per histology**; section-level resampling overstates
   precision relative to a donor-level analysis (Section 6.5c).
10. **Panel-split assumption** (Section 5) is inferred, not documented.
11. **SDRF age/stage are unusable** (invalid M categories; age varies within
    patient), so no age- or stage-adjusted analysis is possible.

## 8. Bottom line

**Does the B7-H3-high niche show altered neighbouring immune abundance, and in
which direction?** In the pre-specified absolute-abundance analysis, yes:
tumour high-CD276 spots have higher neighbouring T cells (+15.4%, CI 1.1-29.0),
B cells (+15.2%, 0.6-28.3), dendritic cells (+28.8%, 9.4-46.9) and neutrophils
(+17.3%, 5.3-29.8), and lower endothelial cells (-16.0%, -25.3 to -4.8).
Adjacent-normal shows uniformly small positive changes (3-13%).

**How confident?** **Weak-to-moderate for a B7-H3-specific immune niche; strong
only for a density/endothelial story.** The absolute immune increases are
largely proportional to a ~12-13% higher total cell abundance around high-CD276
spots and do not survive restriction to interior spots. The composition analysis
leaves one consistent immune signal - dendritic cells +0.5 pp (9/12 sections,
4/5 donors) - and a set of **donor-concordant depletions**:

* **endothelium -2.03 pp** (0/12 sections positive, 0/5 donors),
* **NK cells -0.49 pp** (0/12, 0/5),
* **macrophage -0.40 pp** (2/12, 1/5),
* **monocyte/myeloid -0.23 pp** (2/12, 1/5),
* **mast cells -0.24 pp** (1/12, 0/5),
* plus a **malignant-cell enrichment of +3.79 pp** (12/12, 5/5) and a
  stromal/other depletion of -0.97 pp (1/12, 1/5).

The malignant/endothelial shift is the dominant composition axis; it is a
tumour-versus-stroma contrast, not an immune-cell recruitment signal. There is
**no evidence for selective T-cell enrichment**: the relative T-cell fraction is
essentially unchanged (+0.1 pp; +1.4% with CI crossing zero). The adjacent-normal
panel is weaker still and should be read as a shallow-gradient control, not as
independent confirmation. All of these composition estimates are exploratory and
carry the anticonservative-permutation and 5-donor caveats in Section 6.5.

**What the data support claiming:** high-CD276 regions in LUAD are modestly
denser, endothelial- and stromal-poor, malignant-enriched, and show a small
dendritic-cell enrichment; they are not a selectively T-cell-inflamed niche. The
paper's qualitative "immune-hot B7-H3 niche" pattern is reproduced only in
absolute abundance and is confounded by capture depth and edge effects.

| Deconvolved outputs | `mean_*` and `q05_*` posterior cell abundance for 14 cell types |

The spot abundance matrix is `results/tables/visium_c2l_spot_abundances.parquet`
(47,448 rows x 38 columns: 14 mean abundances, 14 q05 abundances, depth/QC and
CD276 columns). It contains **0 NaN** values; mean abundance range
1.05e-4 to 33.40. The mapping is saved under
`data/processed/c2l_mapping_model_rerun/`.

**Forced deviation from the instruction not to re-map.** The abundance files
inherited from the source run contained **1,328,544 / 1,328,544 NaN** abundance
values: 47,448 spots x 28 columns (14 `mean_*` + 14 `q05_*`). That is 100% of the
abundance columns and 1,328,544 / 1,803,024 = 73.7% of all values in the obs
frame. Revision 1 reported 664,272 / 664,272, which counted only one of the two
posterior statistics; the correction is recorded in the deprecation manifest and
in the run log.

The cause was the export code
`pd.DataFrame(adata.obsm[...], columns=[f"mean_{c}" ...])`, which treats the
prefixed names as a column **selection list** rather than a rename. A 5-epoch
API probe (`code/scripts/visium_c2l_22_export_probe.py`) proved the underlying
obsm values were finite (NaN fraction 0.0) and that the corrected construction
produced 0 NaN. No model checkpoint existed, so the mapping was re-run with the
identical configuration and a corrected export
(`code/scripts/visium_c2l_21_map_sections_rerun.py`). The invalid files are
preserved under `data/processed/deprecated_all_nan_export/`, with a manifest
recording size, shape, NaN count, md5 and the superseding file. **No DE, LIANA,
TCGA or reference-model computation was re-run.** The 4B/4C DE top-gene table
and the CD276 DE summary were rebuilt read-only from the existing 922,455-row DE
result, but the DE model itself was not re-fit.

**CD276 expression context (added in Revision 2).**
`results/tables/scrna_cd276_expression_by_celltype.csv` shows that CD276 is not
tumour-restricted at the transcript level: normal lung macrophages have the
highest detection fraction in the atlas at **36.53%** (3,011 cells, mean log
expression 0.260), comparable to LUAD fibroblasts (**30.84%**, 3,411 cells,
0.329) and SCLC fibroblasts (**35.25%**, 244 cells, 0.401). Any statement that
CD276 is tumour-specific is contradicted by this panel's own table.

**Metadata-integrity warning.** SDRF `age` and `stage` vary between sections of
the same patient and contain invalid AJCC M categories (M2-M5); no patient has a
constant age. These fields are retained verbatim in `.obs` but are unusable as
covariates. Details and the section-level table are in
`results/reports/visium_ingest_qc_log.md` §1.1 and
`results/tables/visium_sdrf_age_stage_integrity.csv`.

## 2. Compute environment and epoch deviations

| Model | Paper | Here | Wall time |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reference regression | 250 epochs, H100 | 250/250 epochs, CPU | 4,586.9 s (18.3 s/epoch) |
| Spatial mapping | 10,000 epochs, H100 | 3,000/3,000 epochs, CPU (original and re-run) | 7,134.4 s original; 7,769.7 s train + 204.5 s export re-run |

* Environment: cell2location 0.1.5, scvi-tools 1.4.2, PyTorch 2.12.0, **CPU
  only**. CUDA use was blocked by the run policy, not by availability of a GPU
  request; no GPU run was attempted.
* **Measured throughput (added in Revision 2).** The mapping has 47,448 spots,
  batch size 4,096, and **12 steps/epoch**. Measured per-step time was
  **0.192 s** in the original run and **0.216 s** in the re-run, i.e.
  **2.3-2.6 s/epoch**. 3,000 epochs therefore cost 6,926-7,770 s (1.9-2.2 h).
  Extrapolating linearly, the paper's 10,000 epochs would have cost
  **23,040-25,920 s (6.4-7.2 h)**, 3.3x longer, for a further ELBO decrease of
  only **0.04%** (Section 3).
* **Epoch rationale.** The reduction from 10,000 to 3,000 epochs is a
  deliberate CPU-budget decision, not an accidental truncation. It is justified
  by the convergence diagnostics: 99.96% of the total ELBO decrease had occurred
  by epoch 2,700 and the last-10% slope was only -137.6 ELBO units/epoch on a
  38.6M ELBO (-0.00036%/epoch).
* **Likely effect.** Posterior abundances should be close to converged, but
  cell-type-specific calibration may differ modestly from a 10,000-epoch model.
  Absolute abundances are not directly comparable to the paper's; within-study
  high-vs-low contrasts are the appropriate readout.

## 6. Neighbourhood analysis: methods, results, robustness

### 6.1 Pre-specified definitions

* B7-H3 level: CD276 **log1p(CP10K)**, not raw counts.
* Stratification unit: **section** (each Visium array is independent; pooling
  spots across sections would let section-level depth/composition drive the
  split; patient-level splitting would mix histologies). high = CD276 above the
  per-section 75th percentile; low = below the 25th; the middle 50% is excluded
  from the contrast but still contributes as a neighbour.
* Neighbourhood: k=6 nearest spots on the Visium hex lattice
  (`array_row`,`array_col`), hard radius **2.05** coordinate units. The six
  physical neighbours are at 1.414 and 2.0; the next ring is >=2.828, so the
  radius returns exactly the true neighbours and never crosses sections. Spots
  with 0 neighbours (130; 37 tumour, 93 adjacent-normal) are excluded; spots
  with 1-5 neighbours (6,002; 2,783 tumour, 3,219 adjacent-normal) use the
  available neighbours.
* Neighbour abundance: unweighted mean posterior abundance of the neighbouring
  spots, self excluded.
* Effect: `(mean_neighbour_high - mean_neighbour_low) / mean_neighbour_low * 100`.
* Uncertainty: 1,000 section-cluster bootstrap resamples (95% percentile CI);
  significance: 1,000 within-section label shuffles (group sizes fixed).
* Reproducibility: seed 42; probe run with 20 permutations/bootstraps logged
  separately (`*_probe20.csv`); full run 23.8 s.

**Stratification reality check.** CD276 is zero in 76.2% of tumour spots
(range 66.3-86.9%) and 92.5% of adjacent-normal spots (83.7-98.2%). Ties at the
lower quartile made **`<q25` empty in 22/22 sections** (`n_cd276_gt_q75` is
15-617 in every section, so the high tail is populated), and the deterministic
rank fallback (top/bottom 25% by CD276 rank) was used throughout. Revision 1
stated the opposite tail; corrected. Consequently: the high group is
CD276-positive in 87.3% of tumour spots (range 52.3-100%) but only **30.0%** of
adjacent-normal spots (7.3-65.2%); the low group is 100% CD276 zero. The
adjacent-normal contrast is therefore weak and near the detection floor.

**Depth balance (labels corrected in Revision 2).** The **mean of the
per-section mean total counts** is 1.76x higher in tumour high vs low spots
(**9,164 vs 5,211**) and 1.28x higher in adjacent-normal (**3,249 vs 2,540**).
The **median of the per-section median total counts** is 7,337 vs 3,676 (2.00x)
in tumour and 2,326 vs 1,945 (1.20x) in adjacent-normal. Revision 1 labelled the
first pair "median"; both quantities are now reported with their correct
statistic. Per-section Spearman CD276 vs total counts averages 0.295 in tumour
and 0.150 in adjacent-normal (section medians 0.311 and 0.161).

`results/tables/visium_neighborhood_edge_spot_sensitivity.csv`

Restricting to spots with exactly six neighbours (interior spots) reverses most

**-29.1**, monocyte +2.2 -> **-25.9**, DC +28.8 -> **+0.03**, mast +8.4 ->

+14.6 -> **-29.7**; NK goes from +3.8 to **-18.5** and endothelial from -16.0 to
**-35.0**, so both remain negative and become more so. This table now covers all
12 immune/context compartments (Revision 1's loop omitted the non-immune types,
so the NK/endothelial sentence could not be checked against it). Adjacent-normal
point estimates stay positive but are less precise (T +9.7, DC +17.2, mast

### 6.5 Multiplicity, spatial autocorrelation and donor clustering

**(a) Multiplicity.** Revision 1 reported raw within-section permutation
p-values with no correction. Revision 2 adds Benjamini-Hochberg FDR within five
pre-declared families, and all three neighbourhood tables now carry
`permutation_p_bh`. Families: absolute abundance = histology x metric (12 tests
per family); additive composition pp = histology x variant x `composition_pp`
(14 tests); relative composition = histology x variant x `relative_composition`
(14 tests); each `total_abundance` endpoint is a single-test family; and the
robustness table also gets a global 48-test pass
(`permutation_p_bh_global48`). Summary counts are in
`results/tables/visium_neighborhood_multiple_testing_summary.csv`.

| Family | n tests | q_BH < 0.05 | min raw p |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tumour absolute abundance (mean) | 12 | 11 | 0.0010 |
| Adjacent-normal absolute abundance (mean) | 12 | 12 | 0.0010 |
| Tumour composition pp, all spots | 14 | 12 | 0.0010 |
| Adjacent-normal composition pp, all spots | 14 | 5 | 0.0010 |
| Tumour composition pp, six-neighbour | 14 | 8 | 0.0010 |
| Adjacent-normal composition pp, six-neighbour | 14 | 0 | 0.126 |
| Tumour relative composition, all spots | 14 | 11 | 0.0010 |
| Adjacent-normal relative composition, all spots | 14 | 8 | 0.0010 |
| Tumour relative composition, six-neighbour | 14 | 5 | 0.0010 |
| Adjacent-normal relative composition, six-neighbour | 14 | 0 | 0.078 |

The correction does not rescue the fragile endpoints: the tumour six-neighbour
composition family retains 8/14 signals driven by the malignant/endothelial/
fibroblast axis, and the adjacent-normal six-neighbour family retains none
(min raw p = 0.126). The plasma-cell absolute increase (p = 0.149) and the
six-neighbour macrophage depletion (q = 0.116) remain non-significant.

**(b) Spatial autocorrelation.** The permutation null shuffles high/low labels
**within a section**, which destroys the spatial autocorrelation of both CD276
and the neighbour abundances. The resulting null is therefore too narrow and the
permutation p-values are **anticonservative**. This is a property no
multiplicity correction can fix. The 1,000-permutation floor is
1/1001 = 0.000999, and 9-11 of the 12 absolute-abundance tests sit exactly at
that floor; those q values should be read as "p <= 1/1001", not as precise
probabilities. The section-cluster bootstrap is the more defensible uncertainty
statement, and it is the one used for the CIs quoted above.

**(c) Donor clustering.** There are only **5 donors per histology**. "3/5" or
"4/5 donors positive" is a descriptive consistency count, not a formal test. The
bootstrap resamples sections, not donors, so it treats sections from one patient
as independent and **overstates precision relative to a donor-cluster analysis**.
The per-donor values are reported in the `donor_pct_changes` column of
`visium_neighborhood_robustness.csv` and in Figure 4E/S5B panel C so a
donor-level analysis can be reconstructed.

---

## 7. Limitations

1. **Depth confounding.** Total and immune abundance correlate with total
   counts (rho 0.40 and 0.30); high-CD276 spots are deeper in tumour
   (mean-of-section-means 9,164 vs 5,211 counts; median-of-medians 7,337 vs
   3,676). Composition and density endpoints mitigate but do not eliminate
   this; a count-matched or depth-regressed design would be stronger.
2. **Sparsity / weak contrast.** CD276 is zero in 83% of all spots; the rank
   fallback was used in 22/22 sections because `<q25` was empty. In
   adjacent-normal, the "high" group is only 30% CD276-positive, so that panel
   tests a shallow gradient and is close to noise.
3. **Edge dependence.** Most tumour immune effects change sign when 1-5
   neighbour spots are excluded; the primary estimate is not robust to spot
   inclusion.
4. **No independent validation.** Results are from one dataset (E-MTAB-13530);
   no held-out section or external Visium cohort was used.
5. **Model approximation.** Mapping used 3,000 epochs (paper 10,000) and CPU;
   the ELBO is flat, but absolute abundances are model-dependent and should not
   be compared across studies.
6. **Reference ELBO unavailable** (logger=False), so reference convergence can
   only be inferred from the reported 250/250 epochs and wall time.
7. **Post-hoc endpoints.** Composition and total-abundance sensitivity analyses
   were added after observing the depth and edge sensitivity; they are
   exploratory, not pre-registered. BH correction reduces but does not remove
   the exploratory-inference problem.
8. **Permutation null ignores spatial autocorrelation**, so p-values are
   anticonservative (Section 6.5b).
9. **Only 5 donors per histology**; section-level resampling overstates
   precision relative to a donor-level analysis (Section 6.5c).
10. **Panel-split assumption** (Section 5) is inferred, not documented.
11. **SDRF age/stage are unusable** (invalid M categories; age varies within
    patient), so no age- or stage-adjusted analysis is possible.

---

## 8. Bottom line

**Does the B7-H3-high niche show altered neighbouring immune abundance, and in
which direction?** In the pre-specified absolute-abundance analysis, yes:
tumour high-CD276 spots have higher neighbouring T cells (+15.4%, CI 1.1-29.0),
B cells (+15.2%, 0.6-28.3), dendritic cells (+28.8%, 9.4-46.9) and neutrophils
(+17.3%, 5.3-29.8), and lower endothelial cells (-16.0%, -25.3 to -4.8).
Adjacent-normal shows uniformly small positive changes (3-13%).

**How confident?** **Weak-to-moderate for a B7-H3-specific immune niche; strong
only for a density/endothelial story.** The absolute immune increases are
largely proportional to a ~12-13% higher total cell abundance around high-CD276
spots and do not survive restriction to interior spots. The composition analysis
leaves one consistent immune signal - dendritic cells +0.5 pp (9/12 sections,
4/5 donors) - and a set of **donor-concordant depletions**:

* **endothelium -2.03 pp** (0/12 sections positive, 0/5 donors),
* **NK cells -0.49 pp** (0/12, 0/5),
* **macrophage -0.40 pp** (2/12, 1/5),
* **monocyte/myeloid -0.23 pp** (2/12, 1/5),
* **mast cells -0.24 pp** (1/12, 0/5),
* plus a **malignant-cell enrichment of +3.79 pp** (12/12, 5/5) and a
  stromal/other depletion of -0.97 pp (1/12, 1/5).

The malignant/endothelial shift is the dominant composition axis; it is a
tumour-versus-stroma contrast, not an immune-cell recruitment signal. There is
**no evidence for selective T-cell enrichment**: the relative T-cell fraction is
essentially unchanged (+0.1 pp; +1.4% with CI crossing zero). The adjacent-normal
panel is weaker still and should be read as a shallow-gradient control, not as
independent confirmation. All of these composition estimates are exploratory and
carry the anticonservative-permutation and 5-donor caveats in Section 6.5.

**What the data support claiming:** high-CD276 regions in LUAD are modestly
denser, endothelial- and stromal-poor, malignant-enriched, and show a small
dendritic-cell enrichment; they are not a selectively T-cell-inflamed niche. The
paper's qualitative "immune-hot B7-H3 niche" pattern is reproduced only in
absolute abundance and is confounded by capture depth and edge effects.

7	* Spot B7-H3 level: log1p(CP10K) of CD276 (NOT raw counts; depth-confounded).
8	* Stratification unit: SECTION. Each Visium section is an independent array
9	  from a single tissue block; pooling spots across sections before quartiling
10	  would let section-level depth/composition drive the split. Patients have up
11	  to 4 sections, so a patient-level split would mix tumour and adjacent-normal
12	  tissue. Sections are therefore stratified independently, and patient is used

15	  the middle 50% is excluded from the high-vs-low contrast (it is still used as

18	  (array_row, array_col) with a hard radius of 2.05 coordinate units. On this
19	  lattice the six physical neighbours sit at 1.414 (diagonal) and 2.0
20	  (same-row); the next ring is >= 2.828. The radius therefore returns exactly

    cols = list(expected_columns)

"""
Multiple-testing correction for the spatial-neighbourhood endpoints.

The primary neighbourhood analysis (script 30) and the post-hoc composition
endpoints (scripts 31/32) report raw within-section label-shuffle permutation
p-values. No multiplicity correction was applied originally. This script adds
Benjamini-Hochberg FDR columns IN PLACE (same filenames, added columns) and
writes a small summary table.

Families
--------
* visium_neighborhood_robustness.csv: one BH pass per (histology, metric) over
  the 12 cell types; plus one global pass over all 48 primary rows.
* visium_neighborhood_composition_pp_difference.csv: one BH pass per
  (histology, variant, statistic) -- 14 tests for composition_pp, 1 for
  total_abundance_pct.
* visium_neighborhood_composition_sensitivity.csv: one BH pass per
  (histology, variant, endpoint) -- 14 tests for relative_composition,
  1 for total_abundance.

Caveat that no correction can fix: the permutation null shuffles high/low
labels WITHIN a section, destroying spatial autocorrelation, so the p-values
are anticonservative and the 1,000-permutation floor is p = 0.000999.

Output
------
the three tables above (extra columns) +
results/tables/visium_neighborhood_multiple_testing_summary.csv
"""
import os
import sys
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from visium_c2l_common import WORK, log_run, checked_frame  # noqa: E402

TAB = f"{WORK}/results/tables"


def bh_fdr(pvals):
    """Benjamini-Hochberg q-values; NaNs are ignored but preserved."""
    p = np.asarray(pvals, dtype=float)
    ok = np.isfinite(p)
    q = np.full_like(p, np.nan)
    n = int(ok.sum())
    if n == 0:
        return q
    idx = np.where(ok)[0]
    order = idx[np.argsort(p[idx], kind="stable")]
    ranked = p[order]
    qvals = ranked * n / np.arange(1, n + 1)
    qvals = np.minimum.accumulate(qvals[::-1])[::-1]
    q[order] = np.clip(qvals, 0, 1)
    return q


def add_bh(df, family_cols, p_col="permutation_p", out_col="permutation_p_bh",
           family_name_col="bh_family"):
    df = df.copy()
    df[family_name_col] = df[family_cols].astype(str).agg("|".join, axis=1)
    df[out_col] = np.nan
    for fam, g in df.groupby(family_name_col, sort=False):
        df.loc[g.index, out_col] = bh_fdr(g[p_col].to_numpy(float))
    return df


summary = []

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- robustness
f = f"{TAB}/visium_neighborhood_robustness.csv"
r = pd.read_csv(f)
assert len(r) == 48, f"expected 48 primary robustness rows, got {len(r)}"
r = add_bh(r, ["histology", "metric"])
# global sensitivity pass across all 48
r["permutation_p_bh_global48"] = bh_fdr(r["permutation_p"].to_numpy(float))
assert r["permutation_p_bh"].notna().all()
assert r.shape[1] == 21, r.shape
r.to_csv(f, index=False)
for fam, g in r.groupby("bh_family"):
    summary.append({
        "table": "visium_neighborhood_robustness.csv", "family": fam,
        "n_tests": len(g),
        "n_p_at_floor": int((g["permutation_p"] <= 0.000999 + 1e-12).sum()),
        "n_bh_q_lt_0.05": int((g["permutation_p_bh"] < 0.05).sum()),
        "min_raw_p": float(g["permutation_p"].min()),
        "min_bh_q": float(g["permutation_p_bh"].min()),
    })

# --------------------------------------------------------- composition pp
f = f"{TAB}/visium_neighborhood_composition_pp_difference.csv"
c = pd.read_csv(f)
assert len(c) == 2 * 2 * 15, f"expected 60 pp rows (14 types + total x 4), got {len(c)}"
c = add_bh(c, ["histology", "variant", "statistic"])
assert c["permutation_p_bh"].notna().all()
assert c.shape[1] == 15, c.shape
c.to_csv(f, index=False)
for fam, g in c.groupby("bh_family"):
    summary.append({
        "table": "visium_neighborhood_composition_pp_difference.csv",
        "family": fam, "n_tests": len(g),
        "n_p_at_floor": int((g["permutation_p"] <= 0.000999 + 1e-12).sum()),
        "n_bh_q_lt_0.05": int((g["permutation_p_bh"] < 0.05).sum()),
        "min_raw_p": float(g["permutation_p"].min()),
        "min_bh_q": float(g["permutation_p_bh"].min()),
    })

# -------------------------------------------------- composition percent change
f = f"{TAB}/visium_neighborhood_composition_sensitivity.csv"
s = pd.read_csv(f)
assert len(s) == 2 * 2 * 15, f"expected 60 sensitivity rows, got {len(s)}"
s = add_bh(s, ["histology", "variant", "endpoint"])
assert s["permutation_p_bh"].notna().all()
assert s.shape[1] == 15, s.shape
s.to_csv(f, index=False)
for fam, g in s.groupby("bh_family"):
    summary.append({
        "table": "visium_neighborhood_composition_sensitivity.csv",
        "family": fam, "n_tests": len(g),
        "n_p_at_floor": int((g["permutation_p"] <= 0.000999 + 1e-12).sum()),
        "n_bh_q_lt_0.05": int((g["permutation_p_bh"] < 0.05).sum()),
        "min_raw_p": float(g["permutation_p"].min()),
        "min_bh_q": float(g["permutation_p_bh"].min()),
    })

SUM_COLS = ["table", "family", "n_tests", "n_p_at_floor", "n_bh_q_lt_0.05",
            "min_raw_p", "min_bh_q"]
out = checked_frame(summary, SUM_COLS,
                    "visium_neighborhood_multiple_testing_summary")
out.to_csv(f"{TAB}/visium_neighborhood_multiple_testing_summary.csv", index=False)
print(out.to_string(index=False), flush=True)

log_run(step="neighborhood_multiple_testing", status="ok",
        detail=(f"BH-FDR added to robustness (48 rows; family=histology x metric), "
                f"composition pp and relative-composition tables (family="
                f"histology x variant x endpoint); {len(out)} families; "
                f"raw permutation p floor = 0.000999"))

# ---------------------------------------------------------- report-side checks
prim = r[r.metric == "mean"]
print("\nTumour mean-block raw p and BH q:", flush=True)
print(prim[prim.histology == "tumor"][
    ["cell_type", "pooled_pct_change", "permutation_p", "permutation_p_bh"]
].round(4).to_string(index=False), flush=True)
print("\nTumour all-spot composition pp raw p and BH q:", flush=True)
print(c[(c.histology == "tumor") & (c.variant == "all_spots")
        & (c.statistic == "composition_pp")][
    ["cell_type", "estimate", "permutation_p", "permutation_p_bh"]
].round(4).to_string(index=False), flush=True)
print("DONE", flush=True)

input.content:
"""
Rebuild the 4B/4C pseudobulk DE top-gene table WITH a direction (sign) filter,
and extract the CD276 row across all contrasts into a small summary.

Why this script exists
----------------------
The delivered SOURCE table `scrna_pseudobulk_de_top_genes.csv` had no surviving
generating script and its "up"/"down" blocks were not sign-filtered: the "up"
block was simply the top-20 significant genes sorted by descending log2FC, so
it contained negative-log2FC genes (e.g. LUAD B cell primary: HINT1 -0.61 ...
ITM2B -1.05), and the LUAD B-cell paired block had identical up/down genes.

Fix: restrict to the DE thresholds already used by 06_pseudobulk_de.py
(padj < 0.05 AND |log2FC| > 0.5), then
  * up   = significant & log2FC > 0, sorted by log2FC descending
  * down = significant & log2FC < 0, sorted by log2FC ascending
and take at most TOP_N per direction. Rank is recomputed within the filtered
block. A `sign_filter_applied` column records the rule.

The large DE CSV (114 MB) is read READ-ONLY from the predecessor run; only the
small summaries are written into this run. Nothing large is copied.

Outputs
-------
results/tables/scrna_pseudobulk_de_top_genes.csv        (rebuilt, sign-filtered)
results/tables/scrna_cd276_de_summary.csv               (CD276 across contrasts)
"""
import os
import sys
import pandas as pd

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from visium_c2l_common import WORK, log_run, checked_frame  # noqa: E402

SOURCE_DE = ("/mnt/beegfs/xqinag/projects/TheVirtualBiotech/runs/"
             "20261021-113551-round-2-of-the-b7-h3-cd276-case-ef6e8b35/work/"
             "single-cell-analyst/results/tables/scrna_pseudobulk_de_luad_sclc.csv")
TAB = f"{WORK}/results/tables"
TOP_N = 20
PADJ = 0.05
MIN_ABS_LFC = 0.5

if not os.path.exists(SOURCE_DE):
    raise FileNotFoundError(f"SOURCE DE table not found (read-only input): {SOURCE_DE}")

use = ["histology", "cell_type", "analysis", "contrast", "gene", "baseMean",
       "log2FoldChange", "lfcSE", "pvalue", "padj", "n_disease_donors",
       "n_normal_donors", "significant"]
de = pd.read_csv(SOURCE_DE, usecols=use)
print("DE rows read:", de.shape, flush=True)
assert len(de) == 15 * 61497, f"unexpected DE row count: {len(de)}"

# Recompute the significance flag from the thresholds rather than trusting a
# stored column (they agree; this makes the filter explicit).
de["sig_recomputed"] = (de["padj"] < PADJ) & (de["log2FoldChange"].abs() > MIN_ABS_LFC)
assert (de["sig_recomputed"] == de["significant"]).all(), (
    "stored significance flag disagrees with padj<0.05 & |log2FC|>0.5")

# ------------------------------------------------------------- CD276 summary
cd = de[de["gene"] == "CD276"].copy()
assert len(cd) == 15, f"expected CD276 in all 15 contrasts, got {len(cd)}"
cd = cd.sort_values(["histology", "cell_type", "analysis"])
cd_out = cd[["histology", "cell_type", "analysis", "contrast", "gene",
             "baseMean", "log2FoldChange", "lfcSE", "pvalue", "padj",
             "significant", "n_disease_donors", "n_normal_donors"]]
cd_out = cd_out.rename(columns={"significant": "significant_at_padj0.05_absLFC0.5"})
cd_out = checked_frame(cd_out, list(cd_out.columns),
                       "scrna_cd276_de_summary")
cd_out.to_csv(f"{TAB}/scrna_cd276_de_summary.csv", index=False)
print("\nCD276 across 15 contrasts:", flush=True)
print(cd_out[["histology", "cell_type", "analysis", "baseMean",
              "log2FoldChange", "padj", "significant_at_padj0.05_absLFC0.5"]]
      .round(4).to_string(index=False), flush=True)
print("\nCD276 significant in any contrast:", int(cd_out[
    "significant_at_padj0.05_absLFC0.5"].sum()), "/", len(cd_out), flush=True)

# ------------------------------------------------------- sign-filtered top genes
sig = de[de["significant"]].copy()
rows = []
for (hist, ct, ana), g in sig.groupby(["histology", "cell_type", "analysis"],
                                      sort=False):
    up = g[g["log2FoldChange"] > 0].sort_values("log2FoldChange", ascending=False)
    dn = g[g["log2FoldChange"] < 0].sort_values("log2FoldChange", ascending=True)
    for direction, block in [("up", up.head(TOP_N)), ("down", dn.head(TOP_N))]:
        for rank, (_, r) in enumerate(block.iterrows(), start=1):
            rows.append({
                "histology": hist, "cell_type": ct, "analysis": ana,
                "direction": direction, "rank": rank, "gene": r["gene"],
                "log2FoldChange": r["log2FoldChange"], "lfcSE": r["lfcSE"],
                "padj": r["padj"], "baseMean": r["baseMean"],
                "n_disease_donors": r["n_disease_donors"],
                "n_normal_donors": r["n_normal_donors"],
            })

TOP_COLS = ["histology", "cell_type", "analysis", "direction", "rank", "gene",
            "log2FoldChange", "lfcSE", "padj", "baseMean", "n_disease_donors",
            "n_normal_donors"]
top = checked_frame(rows, TOP_COLS, "scrna_pseudobulk_de_top_genes")

# Fail-fast: no direction block may contain a wrong-sign gene.
bad_up = int(((top.direction == "up") & (top.log2FoldChange <= 0)).sum())
bad_dn = int(((top.direction == "down") & (top.log2FoldChange >= 0)).sum())
assert bad_up == 0 and bad_dn == 0, (bad_up, bad_dn)
# No gene may appear in both directions of the same block.
dupes = top.groupby(["histology", "cell_type", "analysis", "gene"])["direction"].nunique()
assert (dupes <= 1).all(), f"genes in both directions: {dupes[dupes > 1]}"
top.to_csv(f"{TAB}/scrna_pseudobulk_de_top_genes.csv", index=False)

print("\nSign-filtered top-gene blocks:", flush=True)
print(top.groupby(["histology", "cell_type", "analysis", "direction"])
      .size().to_string(), flush=True)
print("\nwrong-sign rows in rebuilt table:", bad_up + bad_dn, flush=True)

log_run(step="scrna_pseudobulk_de_top_genes_signfiltered", status="ok",
        detail=(f"Rebuilt from SOURCE 922,455-row DE CSV (read-only); "
                f"{len(top)} top-gene rows, up = log2FC>0, down = log2FC<0, "
                f"padj<{PADJ} and |log2FC|>{MIN_ABS_LFC}; up to {TOP_N}/direction; "
                f"CD276 summary written for all 15 contrasts"))
print("DONE", flush=True)

# Deprecated artefacts: all-NaN cell2location export

These two files are retained **for audit only**. They were produced by the first
3,000-epoch cell2location mapping run (2026-10-21 15:08) and every one of their
28 cell-abundance columns is NaN. They must not be used for any analysis,
figure, or claim. The validated replacements are listed under "Superseded by".

## Root cause

The export code built the abundance frame as

```python
pd.DataFrame(adata.obsm["means_cell_abundance_w_sf"],
             index=adata.obs_names,
             columns=[f"mean_{c}" for c in factor_names])
```

The `obsm` DataFrame already has **bare** cell-type names as its columns, so the
prefixed strings were interpreted by pandas as a **column selection list**, not a
rename. No stored column matched `mean_<type>`, so pandas emitted one all-NaN
column per requested label. The underlying posterior values in
`obsm["means_cell_abundance_w_sf"]` were finite (NaN fraction 0.0, confirmed by
`visium_c2l_22_export_probe.py`); only the export was broken. The checkpoint was
not saved (`enable_checkpointing=False`), so the posterior could not be
re-exported and the mapping was re-run. The re-run uses the same configuration
and fixes only the export (`mean_df.columns = [...]` on a copy). See
`code/scripts/visium_c2l_21_map_sections_rerun.py`.

A `checked_frame()` helper in `visium_c2l_common.py` now raises if a constructed
table has an unexpected column set, is empty, or is entirely NaN, so this class
of silent failure fails fast in future runs.

## Deprecated files

### `data/processed/deprecated_all_nan_export/visium_c2l_spot_abundances_all_nan_superseded.parquet`

| property | value |
|---|---|
| bytes | 926,080 |
| md5 | `483c11cc4d56cc2b69e4056162387e46` |
| shape | 47,448 rows x 38 columns |
| abundance columns | 28 (`mean_*` 14, `q05_*` 14) |
| NaN cells | 1,328,544 / 1,803,024 total |
| NaN in abundance columns | 1,328,544 / 1,328,544 (100%) |
| NaN in metadata columns | 0 |
| superseded by | `results/tables/visium_c2l_spot_abundances.parquet` |

### `data/processed/deprecated_all_nan_export/visium_c2l_abundances_small_all_nan_superseded.h5ad`

| property | value |
|---|---|
| bytes | 3,200,679 |
| md5 | `7d54dffeb75e5b1bc6bcf7e3efb1d1f3` |
| obs shape | 47,448 x 38 |
| X shape | 47,448 x 1 (placeholder) |
| abundance columns | 28 (`mean_*` 14, `q05_*` 14) |
| NaN cells | 1,328,544 / 1,803,024 obs cells |
| NaN in abundance columns | 1,328,544 / 1,328,544 (100%) |
| NaN in metadata columns | 0 |
| obsm | `spatial` (47,448 x 2), finite |

## Superseding (validated) files

| property | `results/tables/visium_c2l_spot_abundances.parquet` | `data/processed/visium_c2l_abundances_small.h5ad` |
|---|---|---|
| bytes | 8,898,882 | 7,967,656 |
| md5 | `9c658fce6628de2c080812c425450433` | `e56000389e501355b1d66282e7a04f91` |
| shape | 47,448 x 38 | obs 47,448 x 38 |
| NaN cells | 0 / 1,803,024 | 0 / 1,803,024 |
| producing script | `visium_c2l_21_map_sections_rerun.py` | same |
| model | `data/processed/c2l_mapping_model_rerun/` | same |

## Reporting note on the earlier arithmetic

An intermediate draft of the report described the all-NaN defect as affecting
"664,272 of 1,328,544 values" (47,448 x 14). That is the count for **one**
posterior statistic (mean **or** q05). Both are stored, so the correct count is
47,448 x 28 = **1,328,544 of 1,328,544** abundance values, i.e. 100%, and
1,328,544 of 1,803,024 = 73.7% of all cells in the obs frame. The earlier figure
understated the defect by a factor of two. Revision 2 of the report uses the
corrected numbers.

# Training-history tables: which file to use

This note replaces three 6-byte, header-only CSVs
(`visium_c2l_mapping_history.csv`, `visium_c2l_mapping_history_rerun.csv`,
`c2l_reference_training_history.csv`) that each contained only the column name
`epoch` and no rows. A header-only file is not a training curve and must not be
cited as one. They have been deleted.

## Where the ELBO traces actually are

| model | trace available? | location | rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spatial mapping, original 3,000-epoch run | yes | `logs/c2l_mapping_elbo_metrics_3000epoch.csv` (columns `elbo_train,epoch,step`) | 3,000 |
| Spatial mapping, re-run (corrected export) | yes | `logs/lightning/c2l_mapping_rerun/3000ep/metrics.csv` | 3,000 |
| Reference signature RegressionModel | no | none written | 0 |

The derived statistics (first/last ELBO, last-10% slope, percent of total
decrease reached by 90% of epochs) are in
`results/tables/visium_c2l_training_convergence.csv`; the figure is
`results/figures/figs5_c2l_training_convergence.png`.

## Why the CSVs were empty

`mod.history` in scvi-tools 1.4 is populated from the Lightning logger. In the
re-run script a `CSVLogger` was attached, so the per-epoch values were written by
Lightning under `logs/lightning/`, but `mod.history` itself was empty at the time
the table was written. The reference model was trained with `logger=False`, so no
values were persisted anywhere.

`c2l_reference_training_history.csv` is therefore **not** recoverable: the model
completed 250/250 epochs (Lightning reported `max_epochs=250 reached`; 4,586.9 s,
18.3 s/epoch) but the loss values were never written. No curve is fabricated.

Script `visium_c2l_21_map_sections_rerun.py` now writes the history table only
when it has rows, and logs the Lightning metrics path otherwise.

"""
Audit the SDRF age / disease-staging fields for the 22 sections in this panel.

Why this exists
---------------
The Visium ingest report parsed `Characteristics[age]` and
`Characteristics[disease staging]` straight from E-MTAB-13530.sdrf.txt and copied
them into `.obs['age']` and `.obs['stage']`. A reviewer noticed that within a
single patient the age increments by one year per section and the AJCC M
category increments (M0, M1, M2, ...), which is not biologically possible: M2-M5
are not valid AJCC M categories. These fields describe the section, not the
patient, and must not be used as per-section covariates.

This script re-reads the SDRF (read-only), restricts to the 22 sections used in
the panel, and writes a section-level audit table plus a per-patient summary.
No data are modified; `.obs` columns are left as deposited.

input.content:
"""
Annotate the reconstructed Census batch log and re-derive what is derivable.

Why this exists
---------------
`results/tables/scrna_census_batch_log.csv` was not captured from the tool. It
was written by `source_04_write_batch_log_reference.py`, which hardcodes the b1
row, takes b2/b3 cell counts from `n_cells_expected` in
`data/raw/metadata/luad_batch_definitions.csv`, hardcodes file sizes
(613.15 / 568.37 MB) and asserts `retry_count = 0`. The numbers are consistent
with the merge log, but the file is a reconstruction, not a record of what the
Census tool returned.

This script:
  1. reads the batch log and the predecessor merge log (read-only);
  2. re-derives each batch's returned cell count from the merge log's loaded
     shape -- the only surviving independent evidence;
  3. asserts the log's counts equal those shapes;
  4. adds explicit provenance columns so no reader mistakes the log for a raw
     tool record.

File sizes cannot be re-derived: the batch h5ad files no longer exist anywhere
in the run tree, so the sizes are hardcoded and flagged unverifiable.

Output
------
results/tables/scrna_census_batch_log.csv  (same rows + 4 provenance columns)
"""
import os
import re
import sys

import pandas as pd

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from visium_c2l_common import WORK, log_run, checked_frame  # noqa: E402

LOG_CSV = f"{WORK}/results/tables/scrna_census_batch_log.csv"
MERGE_LOG = ("/mnt/beegfs/xqinag/projects/TheVirtualBiotech/runs/"
             "20261021-113551-round-2-of-the-b7-h3-cd276-case-ef6e8b35/work/"
             "single-cell-analyst/logs/03_merge_qc_downsample.log")

if not os.path.exists(MERGE_LOG):
    raise FileNotFoundError(f"merge log not found (read-only evidence): {MERGE_LOG}")

bl = pd.read_csv(LOG_CSV)
assert len(bl) == 3 and set(bl["batch_id"]) == {"b1", "b2", "b3"}, bl.shape

# "batch01_576f193c_all.h5ad (90384, 61497) obs_names unique: True"
pat = re.compile(r"^(batch0(\d)_\S+\.h5ad)\s+\((\d+),\s+(\d+)\)")
derived = {}
with open(MERGE_LOG) as fh:
    for line in fh:
        m = pat.match(line.strip())
        if m:
            derived[f"b{int(m.group(2))}"] = {
                "merge_log_file": m.group(1),
                "merge_log_n_cells": int(m.group(3)),
                "merge_log_n_genes": int(m.group(4)),
            }
assert set(derived) == {"b1", "b2", "b3"}, f"merge-log batches: {sorted(derived)}"

rows = []
for _, r in bl.iterrows():
    b = r["batch_id"]
    d = derived[b]
    n_log = int(r["n_cells_returned"])
    assert n_log == d["merge_log_n_cells"], (
        f"{b}: log says {n_log}, merge log loaded {d['merge_log_n_cells']}")
    assert int(r["n_cells_estimated"]) == n_log, f"{b}: estimate != returned"
    rows.append({
        "batch_id": b, "dataset_id": r["dataset_id"],
        "disease_scope": r["disease_scope"], "value_filter": r["value_filter"],
        "columns": r["columns"], "layer": r["layer"],
        "n_cells_estimated": int(r["n_cells_estimated"]),
        "n_cells_returned": n_log,
        "n_genes_loaded": d["merge_log_n_genes"],
        "file_size_mb": float(r["file_size_mb"]),
        "success": bool(r["success"]), "retry_count": int(r["retry_count"]),
        "notes": r["notes"],
        "record_type": ("reconstructed: not captured from the tool; written by "
                        "source_04_write_batch_log_reference.py"),
        "cell_count_source": ("n_cells_expected in luad_batch_definitions.csv; "
                              "independently confirmed against merge-log shape"),
        "cell_count_confirmed_by": (f"{os.path.basename(MERGE_LOG)} line "
                                    f"{d['merge_log_file']} -> {n_log} cells"),
        "file_size_source": ("hardcoded; batch h5ad no longer exists, size not "
                             "re-derivable"),
        "retry_count_source": "hardcoded (asserted 0); no retry log survives",
    })

COLS = ["batch_id", "dataset_id", "disease_scope", "value_filter", "columns",
        "layer", "n_cells_estimated", "n_cells_returned", "n_genes_loaded",
        "file_size_mb", "success", "retry_count", "notes", "record_type",
        "cell_count_source", "cell_count_confirmed_by", "file_size_source",
        "retry_count_source"]
out = checked_frame(rows, COLS, "scrna_census_batch_log")
assert len(out) == 3
assert out["n_genes_loaded"].eq(61497).all()
assert out["n_cells_returned"].sum() == 502306, out["n_cells_returned"].sum()
out.to_csv(LOG_CSV, index=False)

print(out[["batch_id", "n_cells_returned", "n_genes_loaded", "file_size_mb",
           "cell_count_confirmed_by"]].to_string(index=False), flush=True)
log_run(step="census_batch_log_annotation", status="ok",
        detail=("Batch log marked as reconstructed; cell counts re-derived from "
                "merge-log shapes (90,384 + 206,186 + 205,736 = 502,306); file "
                "sizes and retry counts flagged as hardcoded/unverifiable"))
print("DONE", flush=True)

# SYNTHETIC FIXTURES — NOT REAL DATA

**Every file under `logs/synthetic_test/` is a synthetic test fixture.** None of
it is derived from E-MTAB-13530, cell2location, or any real specimen. Nothing
here may be cited, plotted, or quoted as a result.

## Why these files exist

The neighbourhood/composition scripts (30-32) and the figure script (41) were
exercised end-to-end on a synthetic abundance table before being run on real
data, to prove the code path and the fail-fast assertions worked. The outputs
were directed here, not to `results/`, so that a code test could not be mistaken
for a result.

## Inventory

| file | what it is |
|---|---|
| `visium_c2l_spot_abundances_SYNTHETIC.parquet` | synthetic spot x abundance table |
| `visium_c2l_abundances_small_SYNTHETIC.h5ad` | synthetic AnnData wrapper |
| `visium_c2l_section_summary.csv` | summary of the synthetic sections |
| `visium_neighborhood_immune_change.csv` | synthetic neighbourhood output |
| `visium_neighborhood_immune_change_synthetic.csv` | same, explicitly suffixed |
| `visium_neighborhood_robustness.csv` | synthetic robustness output |
| `visium_neighborhood_robustness_synthetic.csv` | same, explicitly suffixed |
| `visium_neighborhood_stratification_synthetic.csv` | synthetic stratification output |
| `visium_neighborhood_edge_spot_sensitivity_synthetic.csv` | synthetic edge-spot output |
| `neighborhood_synthetic.log`, `panels_synthetic.log`, `neighborhood_figures_synthetic.log` | run logs of the synthetic test |
| `figures/` | figures rendered from the synthetic tables |

**Caution:** two CSVs and four figures in this directory do **not** carry a
`SYNTHETIC` suffix (`visium_neighborhood_immune_change.csv`,
`visium_neighborhood_robustness.csv`, and everything under `figures/`). Their
location under `logs/synthetic_test/` is the only marker. If you are looking for
deliverable results, use `results/tables/` and `results/figures/`, never this
directory.

## How it was produced

A synthetic abundance table with the same schema as the real
`visium_c2l_spot_abundances.parquet` was generated with a fixed seed (42) and
fed through scripts 30, 31, 32, 40 and 41 by overriding their input paths. The
real analysis was then run on real data. See the synthetic logs for the exact
invocations.

## 6. Neighbourhood analysis: methods, results, robustness

### 6.1 Pre-specified definitions

* B7-H3 level: CD276 **log1p(CP10K)**, not raw counts.
* Stratification unit: **section** (each Visium array is independent; pooling
  spots across sections would let section-level depth/composition drive the
  split; patient-level splitting would mix histologies). high = CD276 above the
  per-section 75th percentile; low = below the 25th; the middle 50% is excluded
  from the contrast but still contributes as a neighbour.
* Neighbourhood: k=6 nearest spots on the Visium hex lattice
  (`array_row`,`array_col`), hard radius **2.05** coordinate units. The six
  physical neighbours are at 1.414 and 2.0; the next ring is >=2.828, so the
  radius returns exactly the true neighbours and never crosses sections. Spots
  with 0 neighbours (130; 37 tumour, 93 adjacent-normal) are excluded; spots
  with 1-5 neighbours (6,002; 2,783 tumour, 3,219 adjacent-normal) use the
  available neighbours.
* Neighbour abundance: unweighted mean posterior abundance of the neighbouring
  spots, self excluded.
* Effect: `(mean_neighbour_high - mean_neighbour_low) / mean_neighbour_low * 100`.
* Uncertainty: 1,000 section-cluster bootstrap resamples (95% percentile CI);
  significance: 1,000 within-section label shuffles (group sizes fixed).
* Reproducibility: seed 42; probe run with 20 permutations/bootstraps logged
  separately (`*_probe20.csv`); full run 23.8 s.

**Stratification reality check.** CD276 is zero in 76.2% of tumour spots
(range 66.3-86.9%) and 92.5% of adjacent-normal spots (83.7-98.2%). Ties at the
lower quartile made **`<q25` empty in 22/22 sections** (`n_cd276_gt_q75` is
15-617 in every section, so the high tail is populated), and the deterministic
rank fallback (top/bottom 25% by CD276 rank) was used throughout. Revision 1
stated the opposite tail; corrected. Consequently: the high group is
CD276-positive in 87.3% of tumour spots (range 52.3-100%) but only **30.0%** of
adjacent-normal spots (7.3-65.2%); the low group is 100% CD276 zero. The
adjacent-normal contrast is therefore weak and near the detection floor.

**Depth balance (labels corrected in Revision 2).** The **mean of the
per-section mean total counts** is 1.76x higher in tumour high vs low spots
(**9,164 vs 5,211**) and 1.28x higher in adjacent-normal (**3,249 vs 2,540**).
The **median of the per-section median total counts** is 7,337 vs 3,676 (2.00x)
in tumour and 2,326 vs 1,945 (1.20x) in adjacent-normal. Revision 1 labelled the
first pair "median"; both quantities are now reported with their correct
statistic. Per-section Spearman CD276 vs total counts averages 0.295 in tumour
and 0.150 in adjacent-normal (section medians 0.311 and 0.161).

### 6.5 Multiplicity, spatial autocorrelation and donor clustering

**(a) Multiplicity.** Revision 1 reported raw within-section permutation
p-values with no correction. Revision 2 adds Benjamini-Hochberg FDR within five
pre-declared families, and all three neighbourhood tables now carry
`permutation_p_bh`. Families: absolute abundance = histology x metric (12 tests
per family); additive composition pp = histology x variant x `composition_pp`
(14 tests); relative composition = histology x variant x `relative_composition`
(14 tests); each `total_abundance` endpoint is a single-test family; and the
robustness table also gets a global 48-test pass
(`permutation_p_bh_global48`). Summary counts are in
`results/tables/visium_neighborhood_multiple_testing_summary.csv`.

| Family | n tests | q_BH < 0.05 | min raw p |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tumour absolute abundance (mean) | 12 | 11 | 0.0010 |
| Adjacent-normal absolute abundance (mean) | 12 | 12 | 0.0010 |
| Tumour composition pp, all spots | 14 | 12 | 0.0010 |
| Adjacent-normal composition pp, all spots | 14 | 5 | 0.0010 |
| Tumour composition pp, six-neighbour | 14 | 8 | 0.0010 |
| Adjacent-normal composition pp, six-neighbour | 14 | 0 | 0.126 |
| Tumour relative composition, all spots | 14 | 11 | 0.0010 |
| Adjacent-normal relative composition, all spots | 14 | 8 | 0.0010 |
| Tumour relative composition, six-neighbour | 14 | 5 | 0.0010 |
| Adjacent-normal relative composition, six-neighbour | 14 | 0 | 0.078 |

The correction does not rescue the fragile endpoints: the tumour six-neighbour
composition family retains 8/14 signals driven by the malignant/endothelial/
fibroblast axis, and the adjacent-normal six-neighbour family retains none
(min raw p = 0.126). The plasma-cell absolute increase (p = 0.149) and the
six-neighbour macrophage depletion (q = 0.116) remain non-significant.

**(b) Spatial autocorrelation.** The permutation null shuffles high/low labels
**within a section**, which destroys the spatial autocorrelation of both CD276
and the neighbour abundances. The resulting null is therefore too narrow and the
permutation p-values are **anticonservative**. This is a property no
multiplicity correction can fix. The 1,000-permutation floor is
1/1001 = 0.000999, and 9-11 of the 12 absolute-abundance tests sit exactly at
that floor; those q values should be read as "p <= 1/1001", not as precise
probabilities. The section-cluster bootstrap is the more defensible uncertainty
statement, and it is the one used for the CIs quoted above.

**(c) Donor clustering.** There are only **5 donors per histology**. "3/5" or
"4/5 donors positive" is a descriptive consistency count, not a formal test. The
bootstrap resamples sections, not donors, so it treats sections from one patient
as independent and **overstates precision relative to a donor-cluster analysis**.
The per-donor values are reported in the `donor_pct_changes` column of
`visium_neighborhood_robustness.csv` and in Figure 4E/S5B panel C so a
donor-level analysis can be reconstructed.

---

## 7. Limitations

1. **Depth confounding.** Total and immune abundance correlate with total
   counts (rho 0.40 and 0.30); high-CD276 spots are deeper in tumour
   (mean-of-section-means 9,164 vs 5,211 counts; median-of-medians 7,337 vs
   3,676). Composition and density endpoints mitigate but do not eliminate
   this; a count-matched or depth-regressed design would be stronger.
2. **Sparsity / weak contrast.** CD276 is zero in 83% of all spots; the rank
   fallback was used in 22/22 sections because `<q25` was empty. In
   adjacent-normal, the "high" group is only 30% CD276-positive, so that panel
   tests a shallow gradient and is close to noise.
3. **Edge dependence.** Most tumour immune effects change sign when 1-5
   neighbour spots are excluded; the primary estimate is not robust to spot
   inclusion.
4. **No independent validation.** Results are from one dataset (E-MTAB-13530);
   no held-out section or external Visium cohort was used.
5. **Model approximation.** Mapping used 3,000 epochs (paper 10,000) and CPU;
   the ELBO is flat, but absolute abundances are model-dependent and should not
   be compared across studies.
6. **Reference ELBO unavailable** (logger=False), so reference convergence can
   only be inferred from the reported 250/250 epochs and wall time.
7. **Post-hoc endpoints.** Composition and total-abundance sensitivity analyses
   were added after observing the depth and edge sensitivity; they are
   exploratory, not pre-registered. BH correction reduces but does not remove
   the exploratory-inference problem.
8. **Permutation null ignores spatial autocorrelation**, so p-values are
   anticonservative (Section 6.5b).
9. **Only 5 donors per histology**; section-level resampling overstates
   precision relative to a donor-level analysis (Section 6.5c).
10. **Panel-split assumption** (Section 5) is inferred, not documented.
11. **SDRF age/stage are unusable** (invalid M categories; age varies within
    patient), so no age- or stage-adjusted analysis is possible.

---

## 8. Bottom line

**Does the B7-H3-high niche show altered neighbouring immune abundance, and in
which direction?** In the pre-specified absolute-abundance analysis, yes:
tumour high-CD276 spots have higher neighbouring T cells (+15.4%, CI 1.1-29.0),
B cells (+15.2%, 0.6-28.3), dendritic cells (+28.8%, 9.4-46.9) and neutrophils
(+17.3%, 5.3-29.8), and lower endothelial cells (-16.0%, -25.3 to -4.8).
Adjacent-normal shows uniformly small positive changes (3-13%).

**How confident?** **Weak-to-moderate for a B7-H3-specific immune niche; strong
only for a density/endothelial story.** The absolute immune increases are
largely proportional to a ~12-13% higher total cell abundance around high-CD276
spots and do not survive restriction to interior spots. The composition analysis
leaves one consistent immune signal - dendritic cells +0.5 pp (9/12 sections,
4/5 donors) - and a set of **donor-concordant depletions**:

* **endothelium -2.03 pp** (0/12 sections positive, 0/5 donors),
* **NK cells -0.49 pp** (0/12, 0/5),
* **macrophage -0.40 pp** (2/12, 1/5),
* **monocyte/myeloid -0.23 pp** (2/12, 1/5),
* **mast cells -0.24 pp** (1/12, 0/5),
* plus a **malignant-cell enrichment of +3.79 pp** (12/12, 5/5) and a
  stromal/other depletion of -0.97 pp (1/12, 1/5).

The malignant/endothelial shift is the dominant composition axis; it is a
tumour-versus-stroma contrast, not an immune-cell recruitment signal. There is
**no evidence for selective T-cell enrichment**: the relative T-cell fraction is
essentially unchanged (+0.1 pp; +1.4% with CI crossing zero). The adjacent-normal
panel is weaker still and should be read as a shallow-gradient control, not as
independent confirmation. All of these composition estimates are exploratory and
carry the anticonservative-permutation and 5-donor caveats in Section 6.5.

**What the data support claiming:** high-CD276 regions in LUAD are modestly
denser, endothelial- and stromal-poor, malignant-enriched, and show a small
dendritic-cell enrichment; they are not a selectively T-cell-inflamed niche. The
paper's qualitative "immune-hot B7-H3 niche" pattern is reproduced only in
absolute abundance and is confounded by capture depth and edge effects.

`work/scientific-reviewer/results/reports/review_round2_full.md` — especially Section 7 (Required recomputations), Section 9 (Bottom line), and Section 4 (live-run consistency). ## Fix list (verify each against the data yourself; do not take the reviewer's numbers on trust either)

### Priority 1 — interpretation-changing
1. **Composition endpoints must cover all 14 compartments.** `code/scripts/visium_c2l_31_neighborhood_composition_sensitivity.py` and `visium_c2l_32_neighborhood_composition_pp.py` currently use 12 of 14 types, so percentage-point differences do not sum to ~0 (tumour −2.820 all spots / −4.811 interior). 2. **Edge-spot loop must cover all cell types.** In `visium_c2l_30_neighborhood_analysis.py` the edge loop iterates `IMMUNE_TYPES` (9) rather than all types; endothelial is absent and NK flips sign. Change to the full `CELL_TYPES`, regenerate `results/tables/visium_neighborhood_edge_spot_sensitivity.csv`, and rewrite the NK/endothelial sentence in the report with the actual regenerated values.
3. **Depth-direction prose is backwards.** The section summary shows median `mean_total_abundance` ~6.42 in tumour vs ~7.14 in adjacent-normal. Verify from `visium_c2l_section_summary.csv` and replace "tumour sections are denser" (and any equivalent) with the correct direction and values.

4. `visium_c2l_43_cd276_stratification_audit.py` labels `median_total_counts_high/low` but computes `.mean()`. Either recompute as true medians or rename to `mean_total_counts_high/low`; regenerate `visium_c2l_cd276_stratification_audit.csv` and update the report.

7. Fix "11 types" → 12 (or whatever the correct count is after checking).
8. Define "ns" explicitly or fix the neutrophil label — the report says "+0.16 (ns)" while `permutation_p = 0.000999` in `visium_neighborhood_robustness.csv`. Re-check every significance label against the delivered p-value and CI.
9. Add to report §6/§7: no multiplicity correction (state raw p-values explicitly, or add BH-FDR across cell types and report both); the permutation null ignores spatial autocorrelation; the section bootstrap ignores donor clustering (sections, not donors, are the resampling unit). State what each implies for inference.
10. Surface the donor/section-concordant depletions in the bottom line: NK, endothelial, macrophage, monocyte/myeloid, mast (with their pp values and "n/N sections, n/N donors" counts). They are currently omitted even though they are the most reproducible findings.
